articles.summary: 1XBET te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta al Alavés y al Villarreal en Mendizorroza este viernes
articles.body: El Alavés recibe al Villarreal en Mendizorroza este viernes en un duelo en el que los babazorros llegan con la moral muy alta tras su comienzo liguero. El conjunto de Quique Sánchez Flores se impuso con contundencia por 3-0 al Getafe, un partido que se decantó definitivamente a su favor tras la expulsión de un jugador azulón antes del descanso. En la segunda jornada, lograron un empate ante el Rayo Vallecano en una salida complicada. Favorito para el partido entre Alavés y Villarreal El Villarreal, por su parte, no ha podido sumar ninguna victoria.Los de Marcelino empataron 2-2 en su visita al Metropolitano ante el Atlético de Madrid, en un partido loco en el que llegaron a disponer de ventaja en el marcador antes de acabar cediendo el empate en los minutos finales. En la primera jornada, obtuvieron el mismo resultado ante el Racing. Con todo esto, las casas de apuestas dan como favorito al Villarreal, con poca diferencia. 1XBET paga la victoria del submarino amarillo a cuota 2.26, por 3.48 del empate y 3.07 del triunfo babazorro. Ambos equipos marcan El mercado de ambos equipos marcan se presenta como una opción a tener muy en cuenta. El Villarreal ha visto puerta y también ha encajado en sus dos partidos disputados, dejando claro que su fase defensiva todavía no está del todo pulida pese al buen nivel de su ataque. El Alavés, aunque resolvió su estreno con un contundente 3-0, no pudo dejar la portería a cero ante el Rayo Vallecano. Con estos antecedentes, la probabilidad de que ambos equipos anoten gana enteros en las apuestas deportivas. 1XBET paga esta opción a 1.63, por 2.17 del caso contrario. Número total de goles (Over/Under) El mercado de goles apunta hacia un partido con cierto componente ofensivo. El Villarreal ha marcado y encajado dos tantos en sus dos partidos de temporada, y el Alavés, nos ha dejado encuentros con 2 y 3 tantos. La suma de ambos perfiles invita a pensar en un partido con goles en los dos porterías. 1XBET sitúa la cuota del +2.5 goles totales a 1.82, por 1.99 del caso contrario. Número total de córners (Over/Under) El mercado de córners también merece atención a la luz de lo sucedido en los partidos de Liga anteriores de ambos equipos. El Villarreal no es, históricamente, un equipo que acumule muchos saques de esquina, ya que su estilo prioriza llegar al área rival por vías más directas que el juego por bandas. La pasada temporada promedió en torno a 4.2 córners por partido, una cifra que se mantuvo en la línea de lo visto en su empate ante el Atlético. El Alavés, por su parte, generó un buen número de córners en su goleada ante el Getafe, favorecido también por la superioridad numérica que disfrutó durante buena parte del choque, lo que le permitió insistir con más centros de los habituales.

articles.title: Texas And Nebraska's Longstanding Volleyball Rivalry Will Renew In Las Vegas
articles.summary: The Nebraska and Texas women's volleyball rivalry spans decades, conferences and national championship matches. On Sunday, the two meet up in the regular season for the first time in a decade.
articles.body: On Sunday afternoon, Texas’ and Nebraska’s women’s volleyball teams will face each in the regular season for the first time in a decade. There wasn't this kind of gap between matches before, however: the Longhorns and Huskers have an intense rivalry spanning decades, tied in part to the creation of the Big 12. At the Players Era Volleyball Showcase in Las Vegas on Aug. 30, the two will jump right into the new season by renewing that rivalry. Nebraska and Texas had their first meeting back in 1981, less than 10 years after each program had begun, and just like on Sunday, it was hosted in neutral territory. The two played a pair of matches in the Oral Roberts Invitational on Oct. 17, with Texas winning both: the Longhorns would eventually be crowned the 1981 champions in the final season playing under the Associate for Intercollegiate Athletics for Women banner (AIAW), while the Huskers’ program was already part of the NCAA at this point; 1981 would mark the lone campaign that the team wasn’t invited to the 20-team NCAA Division I tournament at the end of the regular season, and this despite its fourth-straight unbeaten season in Big 8 conference play. In the 1982 Oklahoma Invitational, Nebraska would collect its first win against Texas, 3-1, but that would be the last victory for the Huskers against the Longhorns until Nov. 5, 1988 — both teams were already powerhouses by then, with Nebraska losing in the national championship in 1986 to Pacific, and Texas winning its second title later in ‘88. Nebraska would once again lose the national championship game in 1989, this time to Long Beach State — it took until 1995 for that to change… and against Texas. That squad, led by First-Team All-American and American Volleyball Coaches Association (AVCA) Co-Player of the Year Allison Weston, was playing for more than just a championship in the moment. It was also playing for bragging rights within a soon-to-be-formed conference. For the 1995 championship, Nebraska was representing the Big 8, and Texas the Southwest Conference, but that was a temporary arrangement: Texas was one of four schools that had committed, back in Feb. 1994, to join the Big 8 and make it the Big 12 in 1996. Nebraska and Texas, two mainstays of women’s volleyball in the midwest, two of the teams that had shown the sport could thrive outside of the West Coast, would now be in the same conference vying for supremacy. Nebraska won 31 straight matches to end the season: the Huskers won the opening game, lost the second to Stanford, and then didn’t taste failure again. Texas was the No. 2 team in the country and had won its two previous national championship games, while Nebraska was hoping that, for the Huskers, the third time would be the charm. It was, and now these two would be in the same conference going forward. And what a run the pair had in the Big 12. Nebraska would win the conference in 1996. Texas would win it in ‘97. The Huskers would then take it in 1998 through 2002, and again from 2004 through 2006 — this stretch was interrupted by a single Big 12 regular season championship by Kansas State, but flanking that were a pair of Nebraska national championships, in 2000 and 2006. In 2007 and 2008, Texas and Nebraska tied for conference championship, then the Longhorns won it outright in ‘09. The Huskers would once again come out on top in 2010 — it was their final year in the Big 12, as now it was their turn to switch conferences. Nebraska joined up with the Big Ten in 2011, and remains there to this day. With Nebraska gone, Texas, somewhat unsurprisingly, dominated the Big 12 in the Huskers’ absence. The Longhorns won 12 of 13 Big 12 conference regular season titles before leaving for the SEC in 2024, with national championships in 2012, 2022 and 2023 and three national title losses, as well. That 2023 championship came against Nebraska, which the Longhorns also defeated in the regional final in the delayed 2020 season as well as in 2021 — the two no longer had conference games, but still played the occasional non-conference matchup and faced each other on the sports’ biggest stage on multiple occasions. All-time, the two have been evenly matched, with Nebraska ahead 25-23 thanks to dominating in Big 12 conference play, 2-12, making up for the initial losing streaks to the Longhorns in the 80s. The pendulum has swung back in Texas' direction, though, with the Longhorns winning seven of the last 10 matchups between the two. Nebraska had its own post-Big 12 success even if direct competition against Texas hasn't gone as well of late, becoming national champions in 2015 and 2017, while losing in the 2018, 2021 and 2023 championship matches. The Huskers were the favorite for the 2025 title, and came into the regional final against Texas A&M undefeated before the Aggies upset them and ended their season, as well as the chance to be the second-ever Nebraska squad to achieve an undefeated championship season, joining the 2000s Huskers. Maybe not coincidentally, the last two undefeated teams standing in Division I last season were Texas and Nebraska, with the Longhorns losing on Halloween to … Texas A&M. Texas’ 2023 victory over Nebraska for the national championship marks the last time the two have faced each other, though, until this weekend, when the No. 2 Longhorns and No. 1 Huskers square off. There is the rivalry to consider, as well as the shocking way 2025 ended for both: both teams lost in their respective regional finals in significant upsets, with 1-seed Nebraska falling to 6-seed Texas A&M and 1-seed Texas to 10-seed Wisconsin. A win against a longtime rival — one the other hasn’t seen in a few years now — would help to wash away the taste of that defeat. But as has so often been the case with the Longhorns and Huskers, only one of these teams is going to walk away on top.

articles.title: Conference Realignment Ahead Of The 2026 College Football Season
articles.summary: Every team that changed conferences ahead of the 2026 college football season.
articles.body: Northern Illinois went west, Sacramento State moved east and the Pac-12 is actually back. Ahead of the 2026 college football season, 22 teams changed conferences. Five of the Group of Six leagues experienced changeover, while the Power 4 remained the same. But two years ago, UCLA, USC, Oregon and Washington joined the Big Ten; Arizona, ASU, Utah and Colorado went to the Big 12; and Stanford and Cal became members of the ACC. Then in 2025, three more teams changed conferences. Now, ahead of the 2026 season, let's do it again. To help you keep up with the trends, and remember who each team will compete against for conference titles, here's a look at who came, who went and who remained in each FBS conference. Pac-12 Additions: Boise State, Colorado State, Fresno State, San Diego State, Texas State, Utah State Holdovers: Oregon State, Washington State After a season in which Washington State and Oregon State were the only two teams representing the Pac-12, the conference has expanded to eight Division I football schools. Colorado State, Utah State, San Diego State, Fresno State and Boise State came over from the Mountain West. Texas State also made the move to the Pac-12 from the Sun Belt Conference. The Pac-12 will include nine schools for college basketball season as Gonzaga came over from the West Coast Conference, but doesn't have a football program. Mountain West Additions: North Dakota State, Northern Illinois, University of Texas-El Paso, Holdovers: Air Force, Hawaii, Nevada, New Mexico, San Jose State, UNLV, Wyoming Losses: Boise State, Colorado State, Fresno State, San Diego State, Utah State After losing five teams to the Pac-12, the Mountain West was replenished with three teams from different conferences. North Dakota State is the headliner. The 10-time FCS national champions come over from the Missouri Valley Football Conference for its debut season in the FBS. Northern Illinois enters from the Mid-American Conference (MAC) and University of Texas-El Paso transfers from Conference USA. Mid-American Conference Additions: Sacramento State Holdovers: Akron, Ball State, Bowling Green, Buffalo, Central Michigan, Eastern Michigan, Miami (OH), Kent State, Ohio, Toledo, UMass, Western Michigan Losses: Northern Illinois The changes to the MAC are simple. Northern Illinois moves to the Mountain West and Sacramento State replaces them, keeping the total at 13. Sacramento State comes over from the Big Sky Conference. Sun Belt Conference Additions: Louisiana Tech Holdovers: Appalachian State, Arkansas State, Coastal Carolina, Georgia State, Georgia Southern, James Madison, Louisiana, Louisiana Monroe, Louisiana Tech, Marshall, Old Dominion, South Alabama, Southern Mississippi, Troy Losses: Texas State Similar to the MAC, the Sun Belt made a one-for-one trade. Texas State joined the Pac-12 and Louisiana Tech replaced them from Conference USA, keeping the Sun Belt's total at 14. Conference USA Holdovers: Delaware, FIU, Jackson State, Liberty, Kennessaw State, Middle Tennessee, Missouri State, New Mexico State, Sam Houston State, Western Kentucky Losses: Louisiana Tech, UTEP Conference USA lost Louisiana Tech and University of Texas-El Paso, and did not replace them as their total dropped from 12 to 10 members. American Athletic Conference Holdovers: Army, Charlotte, East Carolina, Florida Atlantic, Memphis, Navy, North Texas, Rice, South Florida, Temple, Tulane, Tulsa, UAB, UTSA The AAC remained the same heading into the 2026 college football season. It produced a CFP team last year as Tulane earned the 11th seed in the 12-team bracket. Charlotte, FAU, North Texas, Rice, UAB and UTSA joined the AAC as recently as 2023 as the conference has expanded to 14 teams for football. While the Power 4 conferences also avoided any change heading into the 2026 season, it's still worth refreshing who's where. Big Ten Holdovers: Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Maryland, Michigan, Michigan State, Minnesota, Nebraska, Northwestern, Ohio State, Oregon, Penn State, Purdue, Rutgers, UCLA, USC, Washington, and Wisconsin The Big Ten didn't experience any change ahead of the 2026 season. The 2026 season marks the third season in which former Pac-12 schools Oregon, UCLA, USC and Washington will compete in the 18-team Big Ten. Big 12 Holdovers: Arizona, Arizona State, Baylor, BYU, Cincinnati, Colorado, Houston, Iowa State, Kansas, Kansas State, Oklahoma State, TCU, Texas Tech, UCF, Utah, and West Virginia The Big 12 didn't add or lose any teams heading into the 2026 season. The 2026 season marks the third year in which former Pac-12 schools Arizona, Arizona State, Colorado and Utah joined the league. It's also the fourth year of BYU, Cincinnati, UCF and Houston coming over to the Big 12 as the conference has expanded to 16 teams. SEC Holdovers: Alabama, Arkansas, Auburn, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, LSU, Mississippi State, Missouri, Oklahoma, Ole Miss, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Texas A&M, and Vanderbilt The SEC didn't experience any change ahead of the 2026 season. This will be the third season in which Oklahoma and Texas compete in the conference after coming over from the Big 12 to make a 16-team league. ACC Holdovers: Boston College, Cal, Clemson, Duke, Florida State, Georgia Tech, Louisville, Miami, North Carolina, NC State, Pittsburgh, SMU, Stanford, Syracuse, Virginia, Virginia Tech, and Wake Forest The ACC didn't make any moves ahead of the 2026 season. The 2026 season will be the third year in which Stanford and Cal compete in the 17-team ACC.

articles.body:
This week's episode of WWE SmackDown emanates from the Canadian Tire Centre in Ottawa, Canada.

WWE.com has already released the match card and segments for tonight's edition of SmackDown. The show will have at least three matches and two segments, which was already taped back on Monday following WWE Raw.

Here is the announced match card and segments for the show:

Interim WWE Women's Champion Chelsea Green and Tiffany Stratton vs. Nia Jax and Lash Legend in a tag team match.

Jacy Jayne (c) vs. Paige for the Women's United States Championship.

Tatum Paxley vs. Michin in a singles match.

Cody Rhodes to send a message to Randy Orton ahead of their match at Sunday Night's Main Event.

Undisputed WWE Champion CM Punk and Kevin Owens to address Sami Zayn's attack from last Friday's show in Toronto, Canada.

Tonight's episode will start at 8:00 p.m. EST. It is going to be televised on the USA Network in the United States and on Netflix internationally.

Last week on WWE SmackDown, CM Punk retained the Undisputed WWE Championship against Kevin Owens following Sami Zayn 's interference. Zayn hit both Punk and Owens with the Undisputed WWE Title, knocking them out and standing tall to end the show.

Jacy Jayne will be defending her Women's United States Championship for the first time against Paige . Jayne won the title a couple of weeks ago on SmackDown, giving Fatal Influence more gold. Lainey Reid and Fallon Henley are the reigning WWE Women's Tag Team champions.

After making her main roster debut a couple of weeks ago on SmackDown, Tatum Paxley will be wrestling her first match against Michin. Charlotte Flair and Alexa Bliss are expected to be at ringside to even things out with Jade Cargill and B-Fab.

Chelsea Green 's injury story continues with Tiffany Stratton against The Irresistible Forces, while Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton test each other's patience with a potential personal promo battle.

WARNING: These are the full spoilers and results from the taping held on Monday after WWE Raw, courtesy of Fightful and Tom Sherwood on X :

Kevin Owens opens the show. CM Punk interrupts him first, followed by Gunther and then Finn Balor. Owens vs. Gunther vs. Balor in a triple threat match for a shot at Punk's Undisputed WWE Championship was made for the main event.

Nia Jax and Lash Legend def. Chelsea Green and Tiffany Stratton.

Randy Orton and Cody Rhodes have another verbal confrontation. Orton mentioned Cody's wife, Brandi Rhodes, and his mother, Michelle Runnels.

Jacy Jayne (c) def. Paige to retain the Women's United States Championship. Nikki Bella attacked Paige after the match.

Kevin Owens vs. Gunther vs. Finn Balor ended in a disqualification or no-contest after Sami Zayn attacked all three men. CM Punk tried to make the save, but he was also attacked by Zayn, who stood tall to end the show.

WWE will hold another double-taping tonight in Cleveland, Ohio, which will be the August 31 episode of Raw and September 4 edition of SmackDown.

The company is giving its roster a break ahead of Sunday Night's Main Event on September 6, which also begins a busy Latin America tour.

articles.title: Bengals vs. Eagles Tonight: How to Watch, Odds & Prediction
articles.summary: The Cincinnati Bengals can do a closing check on the back end of their roster tonight.They also have an opportunity to finish the preseason unbeaten.Cincinna...
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Bengals can do a closing check on the back end of their roster tonight.

They also have an opportunity to finish the preseason unbeaten.

Cincinnati visits the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field after improving to 2-0 with a convincing 27-9 victory over the Chicago Bears. Philadelphia is headed in the opposite direction at 0-2, though oddsmakers still give the Eagles the edge at home.

Neither team is expected to rely on its regular starters.

Joe Burrow and Cincinnati's first-team offense have gotten their summer work, turning Friday into extended occasion for the reserves who helped control Chicago last weekend.

The Eagles will go that route as well, making the backup quarterback matchup one of the biggest variables in the finale.

How to Watch Bengals vs. Eagles, Latest Odds

Kickoff is scheduled for 8 p.m. ET on Friday, Aug. 28, at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia.

The Bengals' official viewing guide lists CBS as the national television broadcast, with Paramount+ and NFL+ providing streaming options. Cincinnati's radio coverage is available on WCKY 1530, WEBN-FM 102.7 and WLW 700, along with SiriusXM Channel 385.

Philadelphia remains a modest favorite heading into the game.

Sports Illustrated 's Friday DraftKings listing had the Eagles favored by three points, with Philadelphia at minus-155 on the moneyline and Cincinnati at plus-130. The total was 36.5 points.

Prediction markets are displaying confidence in the home team.

Kalshi's Bengals-Eagles market gave Philadelphia roughly a 56% chance of winning this morning, compared to approximately 44% for Cincinnati, and Polymarket was identical.

The market appears to be giving Philadelphia an edge because of its depth at quarterback. Former Bengals starter Andy Dalton and Tanner McKee are competing behind Jalen Hurts , so you've got two experienced options against a reserve-heavy Cincinnati defense.

Bengals Backups Give Cincinnati Upset Chance

Taking Cincinnati isn't fully out of the norm despite the market leaning toward Philadelphia.

The Bengals' backup offense did more than survive against Chicago.

Josh Johnson completed 15 of 23 passes for 156 yards and two touchdowns in the first half of the 27-9 win, via the Bengals' official recap . Cincinnati led 17-9 at halftime before Sean Clifford took over.

Clifford completed 67% of his passes for 126 yards, one touchdown and one interception. The Bengals finished with three passing scores even when resting their regular starters.

That production matters in a preseason finale where the players who created it should once again handle most of the meaningful snaps.

Philadelphia has a legitimate advantage in experience with Dalton and McKee. McKee was particularly sharp against New England, completing 16 of 22 passes for 173 yards and two touchdowns.

The Eagles still lost that game 24-21 and have allowed 24 points in each of their first two preseason contests.

Cincinnati, meanwhile, has won both games while allowing only 23 combined points. Head coach Zac Taylor also made it clear this week that roster spots are available, giving the players on the field much to play for before Sunday's cutdown deadline.

Philadelphia deserves to be a slight favorite because of its quarterbacks and home field. Three points feels less convincing after the way Cincinnati's reserves performed against Chicago.

articles.title: Newcastle Expected to Sell as Five First-Team Players Face Uncertainty: Report
articles.summary: Newcastle United’s incoming transfer business remains the priority before Tuesday’s deadline, but the final days of the window are also expected to bring mov...
articles.body:
Newcastle United's incoming transfer business remains the priority before Tuesday's deadline, but the final days of the window are also expected to bring movement in the opposite direction.

The arrival of Nico Gonzalez from Man City has left Matthias Jaissle with 21 senior outfield players, and that number could increase further if Newcastle lands another one or two attacking targets, as is the club's preference.

According to The Athletic's Chris Waugh , that makes at least some departures likely before the window closes.

"In all likelihood, yes," Waugh reported when addressing whether Newcastle will sanction exits before Tuesday night.

Several senior players have uncertain situations, although Joe Willock increasingly looks likely to remain despite sustained interest from Besiktas. Jacob Murphy has also attracted interest but is considered an important dressing-room leader.

Nick Pope remains available after falling to third choice in Newcastle's revamped goalkeeping hierarchy, but Waugh reported that the 34-year-old could ultimately stay unless a late opportunity — most likely a loan — emerges.

The most intriguing situation surrounds Nick Woltemade. Jaissle said Wednesday that he "expects" the German forward to remain but immediately left the door open to circumstances changing.

"We're talking today (but) football is quite complex and things can change from one day to the other," Jaissle said.

Newcastle's immediate shortage at striker complicates matters after William Osula suffered a foot injury that Waugh expects to sideline him for approximately two weeks. However, signing another attacker or two could facilitate Woltemade's departure.

"A loan appears most likely in that eventuality, given Newcastle's UEFA financial position would be negatively affected should they accept a substantial loss on their £64 million club-record signing of this week last August," Waugh reported.

Newcastle is also expected to sanction several youth loans, as it's been the case during the whole PIF regime. Among those on their (likely) way out are Leo Shahar, Sean Neave, Park Seung-soo, Rory Finneran and Miodrag Pivas, all of whom could temporarily depart Tyneside, while Trevan Sanusi could also leave permanently, per Waugh.

articles.title: Steelers roster spotlight: Can Ryan McCollum secure a backup role?
articles.summary: As the Pittsburgh Steelers move closer to the 2026 season, we’re taking a closer look at every player on the roster, with OL Ryan McCollum up next.
articles.body:
With roster cutdown day looming, Pittsburgh Steelers center Ryan McCollum's backup job may be in jeopardy as the team scrambles to cram as much talent as possible into a 53-man squad .

From now until the start of the regular season, we at Steelers Wire will be analyzing every player on the roster. Here's a look at McCollum and what could be in store for his 2026 season.

Steelers' 2026 schedule revealed: Opponents, dates, primetime games

McCollum, who began his career with the Houston Texans (2021) and Detroit Lions (2021), was claimed off waivers by the Steelers and signed to the practice squad in August 2022. He signed a reserve/future contract with Pittsburgh twice and eventually earned a spot on the initial 53-man roster in August 2024.

Since 2024, McCollum has appeared in 34 games for the Steelers and made three starts. He provided vital depth behind starting center Zach Frazier, but that could soon change depending on how the final roster cuts play out.

McCollum could see Brock Hoffman usurp his role as backup center and, consequently, his spot on the 53-man roster. The Steelers are strapped for roster space and have some very important decisions to make, one of which could be trusting in the versatility of Hoffman, who is capable of starting games at both guard and center, over McCollum.

articles.title: West Virginia announces starting quarterback for 2026 season
articles.summary: The West Virginia Mountaineers have named Oklahoma transfer Michael Hawkins Jr. the starting quarterback, according to Pete Nakos of On3.
articles.body:
The West Virginia Mountaineers have named their starting quarterback. According to Pete Nakos , they've named Oklahoma transfer Michael Hawkins Jr. as their starting quarterback. He'll make his debut against the Coastal Carolina Chanticleers on Sept. 5, 2026.

Hawkins Jr. is entering his redshirt sophomore season. He has just nine games and five starts under his belt from his time at Oklahoma, backing up Jackson Arnold and John Mateer over the past two seasons. In 2024, he came in for an ineffective Arnold and started four games, completing 76 of his 120 passes for 783 yards, three touchdowns, and two interceptions, while adding 204 yards and a touchdown on the ground.

In 2025, Hawkins Jr. started just one game against the Kent State Golden Flashes with John Mateer on the mend. Against Kent State, he completed 14 of 24 passes for 162 yards, three touchdowns, and no interceptions in the 44-0 win.

The Mountaineers are looking for more out of their passing offense. Last season, they earned just 2,267 yards, 10 touchdowns, and 11 interceptions through the air. They cycled through multiple starters after Nicco Marchiol suffered a season-ending injury against the Kansas Jayhawks. They also earned Jacksonville State running back Cam Cook, who won the 2025 Conference USA Player of the Year, from the transfer portal.

articles.title: Ohio State football: Lakota East grad moves from tackle to guard
articles.summary: Austin Siereveld doesn’t care where he plays on the Ohio State Buckeyes offensive line. “Wherever they want me,” he told reporters on Wednesday, Aug. 26, at...
articles.body:
Austin Siereveld doesn't care where he plays on the Ohio State Buckeyes offensive line.

"Wherever they want me," he told reporters on Wednesday, Aug. 26, at the Woody Hayes Athletic Center in Columbus.

Coach Ryan Day expects Siereveld, a 2023 Lakota East High School graduate, to start at right guard after playing left tackle last season. In a press conference Monday, Day said that was the current plan. It wouldn't be finalized until later in the week.

"He obviously spent a lot of time at tackle last year," Day said.

Now the 6-foot-5, 327-pound Siereveld is working on the interior of the line, Day said, and "getting more and more comfortable" as the Sept. 5 opener against Ball State approaches.

The other expected starters on the line are left guard Luke Montgomery, center Carson Hinzman, left tackle Ian Moore and right tackle Phillip Daniels. Everyone but Moore, who made one start in 2025, started most of last season.

One of the backups at guard is Wayne grad Joshua Padilla, who appeared in 13 games last season and started against Miami in the College Football Playoff.

Siereveld has built chemistry with the other linemen. He has a natural connection with Daniels, a Princeton High School graduate, because Siereveld grew up not far away in Liberty Township. Siereveld played next to Hinzman when Siereveld played guard two years ago.

"Now we can look at each other," Siereveld said of his fellow linemen, "and we already know what's going to happen."

This will be the third straight year Siereveld, Daniels and Hinzman have started together.

"It's very uncommon to have your three interior guys play for three years together," Siereveld said, "and we've got to take advantage of that. The connections we have are unreal. We vibe. We click."

Siereveld has played all over the line in his Ohio State career. After redshirting as a freshman in 2023, he played left and right guard in 2024, appearing in 16 games and making seven starts.

Last season, Siereveld was expected to play guard but was moved to left tackle. He made the All-Big Ten second team.

I thought I'd always be at guard," Siereveld said before the 2025 season, "but I'm just working on my craft every day. The coaches are helping me out when I ask questions. I'm just working every single day to try to be the best player I can be.

Siereveld started all 14 games for a team that finished 12-0 in the regular season before losing to Indiana in the Big Ten championship game and to Miami in the playoff quarterfinals. He totaled 810 snaps after playing 577 snaps in 2024.

"Last year was the first year I played one position all year," Siereveld said, "and I was just so comfortable."

"I was so used to guard in my first two years," Siereveld said. "Stepping out there was a challenge at first. Getting as many reps as possible, each week I was getting better and better."

The decision to move Siereveld back to guard was made so Ohio State could start junior Moore at left tackle.

Siereveld told offensive line coach Tyler Bowen he hated right guard because he was so used to left tackle, but his feeling soon changed.

"As you get more and more reps, you get more used to it," he said, "and I got comfortable with it."

For the second straight year, Siereveld will serve as a captain. Day announced seven captains for the 2026 season on Aug. 22. The others are wide receiver Brandon Inniss, defensive end Kenyatta Jackson Jr., safety Jaylen McClain, linebacker Payton Pierce, quarterback Julian Sayin and wide receiver Jeremiah Smith.

"This is a significant day for our program," Day said in a press release. "We have seven captains this year, the seventh time in Ohio State football history that we have had that many or more. Being voted a captain is one of the greatest honors in this program because it comes directly from your teammates. This group represents our team well, with leaders from different position groups, backgrounds, and experiences. All seven are returning players, including two captains from last year, and they understand our standard and what it means to carry our culture forward."

Only Siereveld and Inniss are returning captains. Players vote for captains and can choose from juniors, seniors or fifth-year players.

"It means a lot," Siereveld said. "Especially being from Ohio, it means even more. Shoutout to all the guys out there for trusting me and voting for me."

articles.title: Scunthorpe Utd would 'embrace' Tinie Tempah visit
articles.summary: A campaign is under way to get the rapper to the town after he referred to it in one of his hits.
articles.body:
The co-owner of Scunthorpe United FC says the club would "love to embrace" rapper Tinie Tempah if he were to visit the town.

His 2010 number 1 hit Pass Out included the lyrics "I been Southampton, but I've never been to Scunthorpe", and efforts are being made to put that right.

An online campaign to get him to perform in North Lincolnshire was started recently by local fan Ben Johns.

Speaking to BBC Newsnight earlier this month, the rapper said he thought "this is the time" to visit the town.

"I've said I'm more than excited to come to Scunthorpe," he said.

"I'm happy to add that date to my tour. But we need a certain amount of pre-saves on the new album.

"If we can achieve that I will – just like that, at the click of a finger – add a Scunthorpe date, and we'll see you there in November or December."

Michelle Harness, the football club's chairwoman, told BBC Radio Humberside that "we'd love to embrace" a show by Tinie, although the club would need to explore how best to host the gig at The Attis Arena.

She said: "I don't know how they run big concerts at big stadiums. They put something over the pitch, they raise it off the actual grass... We wouldn't do anything without protecting the pitch."

Johns, who is behind the campaign and is from Scunthorpe, previously told BBC Radio Humberside that it "feels like it's been a story 16 years in the making".

"I don't really know where we could have the venue. There's a really great independent venue in Scunthorpe called Café Indie, but I think the demand is going to be so big we might need to have it at The Attis Arena... So many people want to come!"

articles.title: 2026 Tour Championship: Cameron Young makes quick turnaround at East Lake, shoots 62
articles.summary: Playing early and playing alone has been advantageous so far the Tour Championship, a scenario Cameron Young benefitted from Friday. Young carded a 62, match...
articles.body:
Cameron Young birdied seven out of nine holes during the middle of Friday's second round in Atlanta, charging up the Tour Championship leaderboard a day removed after being tied in last place .

He eagled at par-5 18th to complete an 8-under 62 and temporarily catch first round leader Min Woo Lee , who completed his first hole a few minutes before Young's day ended.

It was a remarkable turn of event for Young, who was just three players in the field to card an opening round 70. He bogeyed three of his first five holes and never recovered Thursday, despite a Round 1 scoring average that dipped below 67.

Round 2 was the complete opposite for the 2026 Players champ , who was the first player off the tee and posted a 30 on his front nine behind a string of three straight birdies from holes Nos. 4 through 6.

He went birdie-birdie to open his back nine — opening the possibility for a 60 or sub-60 score — before running into trouble at the par-4 12th. His first bogey of the round dropped Young to 6 under, where he stayed for more than an hour thanks to five consecutive pars.

The TOUR Championship brings this season's top players to East Lake Golf Club in Atlanta to crown the 2026 FedExCup champion.

Then came the big moment to finish the round — an eagle putt, perhaps his best of the season.

Young played alone Friday, just like Lee did a day earlier. Lee was playing with J.J. Spaun on the front nine, when the 2025 U.S. Open champ withdrew due to a right shoulder injury .

Lee went on to play well without him, tying a career-low mark for a single round with an 8-under 62.

He went par-par to open his second round, leaving him tied at 8 under with Young as of 2:30 p.m. Friday.

articles.title: WWE Rumors on The Rock vs. Roman Reigns, Bayley's Contract and New Day & Ilja Dragunov in AEW
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe and All Elite Wrestling.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe and All Elite Wrestling.

Doubt Reportedly Mounting for The Rock vs. Reigns at WM 43

The Rock vs. Roman Reigns has arguably been the biggest and most-talked-about dream match in wrestling for the past several years, but there is reportedly still no sign that it will come to fruition any time soon.

According to Dave Meltzer of Wrestling Observer Radio (h/t Cain A. Knight of Cageside Seats), it is far from certain that the Saudi Arabian government would be willing and able to meet The Rock's asking price to have a match at WrestleMania 43 in Saudi Arabia.

Meltzer added that "there's definitely people behind the scenes" who believe "the never-ending money supply" provided by Saudi Arabia to WWE and other sports and entertainment organizations "may not be never-ending anymore."

On top of that, Vin Diesel recently told Jack Dunn and Marc Malkin of Variety that filming for the latest installment of the Fast & Furious movie franchise, Fast Forever , will begin filming in December.

If that is the case, it could complicate The Rock's path to WrestleMania 43 since he is set to be one of the stars of Fast Forever .

While it may not be at WrestleMania 43, The Rock hinted he may return at a future installment during an appearance on The Morning Shift (4 minute mark of the video):

As much as fans would undoubtedly love to see The Rock vs. Reigns on the WrestleMania stage, it isn't as if WWE is without options should The Rock not commit to participating in WrestleMania 43.

The most obvious option for Reigns if The Rock is off the table is Oba Femi, who called Reigns out after beating Brock Lesnar at WrestleMania 42.

Bayley Reportedly Expected to Re-Sign with WWE

Despite speculation about her potentially jumping ship to AEW, it is reportedly expected that Bayley will re-sign with WWE.

According to Meltzer (h/t Wrestle Features ), Bayley is "pretty much a lock" to sign a new WWE deal.

Meltzer (h/t Derek Holloway of Ringside News) previously said, "The frequent mentions of [Bayley] on Raw this week would indicate to me that they expect her back. If they believed she might be leaving, they would not mention her name."

Bayley has indeed been mentioned often in recent weeks by Lyra Valkyria, who beat Bayley in what was her last televised match at Saturday Night's Main Event.

Valkyria has been bragging about running Bayley out of the company, and based on WWE's usual practices, the company wouldn't necessarily draw attention to Bayley if it felt she was going to leave for AEW or another promotion.

While the exact status of Bayley's contract talks with WWE are unknown, Bryan Alvarez of Wrestling Observer Radio (h/t WrestlingInc.com's Julien D'Alessandro ) recently said he had been told by a source that her contract expires in January.

That means WWE still has about four months to get Bayley locked into a long-term agreement if that hasn't happened already.

Bayley has links to AEW with longtime friend Mercedes Mone being the most obvious example, but she is also deeply rooted in WWE, having been with the company since 2012.

AEW's Reported Interest in New Day, Dragunov

With AEW's biggest pay-per-view of the year, All In, set for Sunday, rumors are running rampant regarding some potential new additions to the roster.

According to WrestleVotes on Fightful Select (h/t Knight ), people in AEW expected New Day to make their debut for the company at All In, which they are now free and clear to do following their WWE departure nearly four months ago.

Alvarez (h/t Knight ) added that Kofi Kingston and Xavier Woods will most likely be part of the Trios Roulette Royale as a mystery partner for Swerve Strickland.

That match is scheduled to start on the pre-show before spilling over into the start of the pay-per-view, and having New Day debut as surprise entrants would be a strong way for AEW to kick off the show.

Another wrestler believed to be on AEW's radar is Ilja Dragunov, who recently left WWE as well.

Per WrestleVotes on Fightful Select (h/t Knight ), a source within AEW expects the company to attempt to sign Dragunov soon, if it hasn't done so already.

Meanwhile, WWE sources told WrestleVotes that Dragunov is not expected back with WWE any time soon.

PWInsider.com (h/t WrestlePurists ) reported that Dragunov allowed his WWE contract to expire in order to become a free agent, rather than re-signing with the company.

That means no 90-day non-compete clause applies to him, and he could conceivably debut for AEW at All In, potentially in the Casino Gauntlet match, should he decide to sign with the promotion.

articles.title: Coaching Changes That Will Impact The 2026 College Football Season
articles.summary: Here's everything to know about the coaching carousel heading into the 2026 college football season.
articles.body: The coaching carousel ran rampant this past offseason. Lane Kiffin jumped from one SEC team to another. Kyle Whittingham will try to restore Michigan's prowess. A handful of top programs are betting their future on up-and-coming former Group of Six coaches. Coaching changes will affect the 2026 college football season. Here's a look at the moves that could have the greatest impact. Lane Kiffin (Ole Miss → LSU) Kiffin left Ole Miss in November after leading the Rebels to an 11-1 record. After five years at Ole Miss, Kiffin's departure created chaos around a feel-good College Football Playoff run for the Rebels. Kiffin hopped to SEC rival LSU, his fifth stop as a Division I head coach and third in the SEC. Kiffin recruited Arizona State transfer QB Sam Leavitt to join him as he tries to revitalize a Tigers' program that hasn't won the SEC since 2019 with Joe Burrow in the pocket. Bob Chesney (JMU → UCLA) Chesney followed the footsteps of Curt Cignetti, going from the Sun Belt's James Madison to the Big Ten, and he settled at UCLA. In 2025, Chesney led the Dukes to a 12-1 season, including a Sun Belt title and a CFP appearance. He'll try to turn around a Bruins program that went 8-16 under DeShaun Foster in its first two seasons of B1G football. UCLA's roster consists of 63 newcomers, 42 of them transfers – 10 of which came from JMU with Chesney. Kyle Whittingham (Utah → Michigan) Whittingham succeeds Sherrone Moore at Michigan, where he'll try to clean up a mess and help the Wolverines return to the form they were in when they won the 2023 national championship. Whittingham spent 23 years as Utah's head coach, leading its program to two Pac-12 championships. James Franklin (Penn State → Virginia Tech) After James Franklin's 12-year run at Penn State abruptly ended in the middle of last season, he landed at Virginia Tech a month later. Franklin got right to work, flipping 10 Penn State commits to Virginia Tech. Franklin still has a tall task at hand as the Hokies haven't won 10 games since 2016. Matt Campbell (Iowa State → Penn State) After a lengthy search, Penn State replaced Franklin with Matt Campbell. Campbell was known for doing a lot with a little at Iowa State, where he qualified for eight Bowl Games in 10 seasons. Now with the Nittany Lions, he'll have a few more resources backing him up. Campbell took Cyclones quarterback Rocco Becht to help set a foundation at State College. Jon Sumrall (Tulane → Florida) Sumrall parlayed Tulane's CFP appearance into a head coaching position with Florida. Sumrall has a rocket strapped to his career, as he got his first Division I head coaching gig with Troy in 2022, and four years later is in the SEC. Florida hasn't won 10 games since 2019. Pete Golding (Elevated At Ole Miss) Golding took over at Ole Miss ahead of the CFP after Lane Kiffin left for LSU at the end of the 2025 regular season. Golding lifted Ole Miss to the semifinals with wins over Tulane and Georgia, before the Rebels lost to Miami (FL). Golding retained quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, and will try to build on a season in which the Rebels won the most games in program history. Will Stein (Oregon → Kentucky) Stein earned his first Division I head coaching gig with Kentucky after three seasons as Oregon's offensive coordinator. He's taking on an uphill battle as Kentucky's athletics department prioritizes basketball, and its football team has only won 10 games twice in the last 10 years. Stein, though, has the gumption to fundraise, and will have to rely on that as he tries to find consistent success in Lexington. Alex Golesh (USF → Auburn) Golesh jumped from G6 to P4 after lifting South Florida to a third straight winning season in 2025. He'll take over an Auburn program that hasn't had a winning season since the COVID-19 shortened 2020. Golesh took USF quarterback Bynum Brown with him to Auburn, and together they'll try to compete in the SEC. Brian Hartline (Ohio State → USF) Hartline has become famous for building Ohio State into WR-U. Being the head coach of a G6 program is a whole 'nother task. Hartline will have to prove that his positional development chops translate to overseeing an entire roster at a USF program that's had three straight winning seasons.

articles.title: Beau Greaves loses thriller to Cross on European debut
articles.summary: Beau Greaves narrowly loses 6-5 to Rob Cross on her European Tour debut in the Hungarian Darts Trophy.
articles.body:
Beau Greaves narrowly lost 6-5 to Rob Cross on her European Tour debut in the Hungarian Darts Trophy.

The 22-year-old beat Tom Bissell last month to become the first woman to qualify for a PDC European Tour event.

England's Cross won the opening leg in Budapest before Greaves took a 2-1 lead in a thrilling encounter.

They continued exchanging legs as Greaves went 5-4 up to close in on becoming the first women to win a European Tour match.

Requiring 70 to win the match in the deciding leg, Greaves made two poor errors and was punished by Cross.

The narrow defeat continues a remarkable rise after she became the first woman to win a PDC ranking title in April.

Luke Humphries and Michael van Gerwen will enter the tournament in the second round, while world champion Luke Littler is not playing.

articles.title: Haaland and Cherki doubles send Man City to EPL win at Crystal Palace
articles.summary: Manchester City make it back-to-back wins to start the Premier League season as Crystal Palace slip to another defeat.
articles.body:
Erling Haaland and Rayan Cherki both scored twice as Manchester City stormed to a 4-1 win at Crystal Palace in the English Premier League on Friday.

City led through Haaland’s header at the break at Selhurst Park, but stormed clear with a wonderful dribble and slotted finish from Cherki, before he doubled his tally with a deflected effort from the edge of the box.

Yeremy Pino had given Palace some hope from a freekick in between Cherki’s strikes, which came back off the woodwork and rebounded in off Gianluigi Donnarumma in City’s goal – an unfair own goal awarded against the keeper.

Haaland sealed the win with a drilled left-footed finish after he was put through by Phil Foden, who contributed two assists on the night.

“It was a step up, but we will make it,” Haaland told Sky Sports, before adding the team is starting to find their way under new manager Enzo Maresca. “It is a new manager but most of use have been playing together. We have to trust the new manager and what he wants us to do.”

“We have so many good players and we have to fit everyone in. We all have to work hard, and Foden too, this is the step in the right direction for us.”

City had stuttered in their opening game of the season on Sunday, as they came from behind to beat Bournemouth with a late salvo – inspired by two assists from Cherki, who started that match on the bench.

The France playmaker responded to the snub in emphatic style with that performance and his Player of the Match display at Palace.

“With Pep we had a big story. Now we start another one and we are here for that,” Cherki told Sky Sports.

“I want to show Enzo I can play balls for Haaland, and help him score goals.”

On his brilliant individual effort for City’s second goal, Cherki added: “When Haaland gave me the ball, then I did my thing. But I just want to give him goals.”

In a glimpse into what City hope is a bright future after Guardiola, teenage Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi, signed from Lille for 86 million pounds ($116m) this week, came off the bench for his debut in the closing minutes.

For Palace, it is back-to-back defeats to start their campaign following a 2-0 reverse at Everton.

Season 3 figures to be a star-studded year as well, with Bueckers and more of the league's premier players already on board.

articles.title: Cale Makar, Avalanche Agree to Historic Contract Extension to Be NHL's Highest-Paid Player Ever
articles.summary: The Colorado Avalanche are making two-time Norris Trophy winner Cale Makar the highest-paid player in the NHL.
articles.body:
The Colorado Avalanche are making two-time Norris Trophy winner Cale Makar the highest-paid player in the NHL.

The Avalanche and Makar announced Friday they have agreed to an extension.

The deal is an eight-year, $163.2 million deal worth a record $20.4 million AAV, per Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman and the Denver Gazette 's Evan Rawal .

The news comes after Avalanche general manager Joe Sakic said earlier this summer Makar would "finish his career" with Colorado.

The contract, which beats the previous record of $18.8 million AAV set by San Jose Sharks star Macklin Celebrini, will keep Makar in Denver through his age-35 season in 2034-35.

Makar is heading into his eighth regular season in Colorado, where he played a key role in the Avs' run to the 2022 Stanley Cup.

He was previously set to hit free agency in 2027 after playing out the final season of his previous six-year, $9 million AAV contract.

That tied for 12th in terms of average salary among all NHL defensemen last season, per Spotrac .

Makar will now rank No. 1 after finishing the 2025-26 season as a Norris Trophy finalist for the sixth straight season.

He earned his raise after ranking third both among Avalanche skaters and all NHL defensemen with 79 points (20 goals, 59 assists) in 75 games.

Makar played key roles on both the Avs' penalty kill, on which he ranked sixth on the team in ice time, and on the power play, where he ranked third.

The Avalanche spent 45.3 percent of their time in the offensive zone when Makar was on the ice, higher than the league average of 42.3 percent, per NHL Edge .

NHL Edge reports Makar also ranked in the 99th percentile of NHL defenders with a top skating speed of 23.68 miles per hour.

His impact on the Avalanche was made even clearer during the playoffs, during which the Avs struggled and were eventually limited from the Western Conference Final in part because of Makar's injury limitations.

The Avalanche will now hope having Makar and Nathan MacKinnon under contract for the next few seasons will allow this team to contend for another Stanley Cup in the near future.

The Avs also have Devon Toews signed through the 2030-31 season, giving the team top defensemen on both the right and left side of the blue line.

Colorado could now look to either run things back with Toews and Makar at the top or shuffle pairings after re-signing left-side defensemen Brett Kulak and Josh Manson this offseason.

Makar was selected by the Avs with the No. 4 pick of the 2017 draft and has since established himself as one of the league's best offensive blueliners. No defenseman has recorded more goals (136) or points (507) since Makar made his regular-season debut in 2019.

articles.title: Hungarian Darts Trophy: Beau Greaves just loses out to Rob Cross in last-leg decider on European Tour debut
articles.summary: Beau Greaves became the first woman to play in a PDC European Tour event after qualifying for the Budapest tournament last month; Greaves and Rob Cross both averaged over 100 in first-round match with Cross edging the deciding leg after errors from opponent when left with chance on 70
articles.body:
Rising star Greaves, 22, made history by becoming the first woman to compete in a PDC European Tour event after qualifying last month for both this weekend's tournament in Budapest and the Czech Darts Open in September.

And she pushed the experienced Cross to a deciding 11th leg in a thrilling tie on Friday evening, averaging an impressive match-best of 104.88 and hitting five 180s.

Cross, who played well himself with an 101.90 average, had made a flying start to the match with a 170 first-leg checkout but Greaves, who is dominating the PDC women's series, quickly showed her competitiveness and took the next two legs.

She moved one more leg away from victory at 5-4 but Cross hit back to win the final two, with Greaves left to rue mistakes with her first two darts in the decider when left with 70.

Cross seized his first chance at victory by taking out 61, with the 35-year-old to now play Luke Woodhouse in Saturday's second round.

"Beau is brilliant," said Cross. "She is going places.

"She has been phenomenal on the ProTour, and I think when she learns her trade on the big stage, she's going to do more.

"I feel really happy with my set-up at the minute. I think I can do great things, but it's down to me to prove it."

Earlier on Friday evening and Hungary's own Laszlo Kadar had caused the upset of the night by beating Daryl Gurney 6-5. Kadar will now play Jonny Clayton in Saturday's second round.

Defending champion Niko Springer is also into round two after a comfortable 6-1 win over Maik Kuivenhoven, while former winners Joe Cullen and Dave Chisnall are also through after 6-3 victories against Adam Leek and Andras Borbely respectively.

Luke Humphries, Gian van Veen and Michael van Gerwen all enter the tournament in round two.

Humphries, who returned to winning ways with victory at Players Championship 28 in Leicester on Wednesday, will face an intriguing test against World Matchplay semi-finalist Dirk van Duijvenbode after the Dutchman crushed David Pisek 6-1.

articles.title: Cale Makar, Macklin Celebrini and the NHL's Highest-Paid Players After Avs Star's Historic Contract
articles.summary: The Colorado Avalanche have officially reset the top of the NHL market.
articles.body:
The Colorado Avalanche have officially reset the top of the NHL market.

Cale Makar made league history Friday when he agreed to a reported eight-year, $20.4 million AAV extension.

That contract beat out the previous record set by the San Jose Sharks, which signed Macklin Celebrini to a five-year, $18.8 million AAV deal earlier this offseason.

Here's a look at the players set to be the top five highest-paid in the NHL once their new deals kick in.

The NHL confirmed in May the salary cap would increase by $8.5 million ahead of the 2026-27 season.

The highest salary allowed under that limit is $20.8 million. The Avs are paying Makar just below that after the two-time Norris Trophy winner put together a sixth straight point-per-game campaign last season.

The Minnesota Wild's Kirill Kaprizov was the first player in this top five group to make NHL history with the eight-year, $17 million AAV extension he signed ahead of the 2025-26 season.

The market has been reset multiple times amid a busy offseason.

The Philadelphia Flyers submitted a five-year $18 million AAV offer sheet for Leo Carlsson, which was matched by the Anaheim Ducks in July to briefly make Carlsson the NHL's highest-paid player.

Connor Bedard signed his five year, $15 million AAV extension later that month, followed shortly afterward by Celebrini and his record deal.

The NHL salary cap is projected to climb by another $9.5 million before the 2027-28 season, which would set the maximum player salary around $22.7 million.

One extension-eligible player who could potentially rank near the top of the market is reigning Hart Trophy winner Nikita Kucherov, who is currently heading into next season on an expiring deal with the Tampa Bay Lightning.

Another candidate for a significant extension could be Dallas Stars winger Jason Robertson, who signed to a one-year agreement in July but will be looking for a long-term deal on his next contract.

The biggest upcoming contract negotiations could potentially involve Edmonton Oilers star Connor McDavid. After signing a below-market-value $12.5 million AAV deal that runs through the next two seasons, McDavid could reset the market should he seek higher pay after the 2027-28 campaign.

articles.title: Super League: Leeds Rhinos return to the top of the league with win at St Helens as Huddersfield and Catalans also triumph
articles.summary: Leeds return to the top of Super League ahead of Wigan after a comfortable 34-6 away win at St Helens; Saints still outside play-off spots with two matches to go; watch three more matches, including Hull FC vs Warrington Wolves at 5.30pm, live on Sky Sports+ on Saturday
articles.body:
The Rhinos scored six tries in a dominant display at the Brewdog Stadium that halted Saints' recent resurgence and left the Merseysiders outside the play-off places with two games remaining.

Chris Hankinson gave Brad Arthur's side an early lead before two tries in quick succession from Cameron Smith and Harry Newman put them in complete control late in the first half.

Further touchdowns by Ryan Hall, Ash Handley and Brodie Croft wrapped up a comprehensive win while the influential Jake Connor landed five conversions.

It was a strong response by the Rhinos after Wigan crushed champions Hull KR to move ahead of them on Thursday night.

They controlled the game from the outset, frustrating Saints after interim coach Eamon O'Carroll had overseen back-to-back wins to revive their hopes of forcing their way into the top six.

Leeds' early pressure paid off after seven minutes when Connor sent Hankinson over for the opening try with a cleverly delayed pass.

Cooper Jenkins thought he had extended the Rhinos' lead soon after, but his effort was ruled out for a knock-on in the build-up.

Saints gradually began to get into the game but Deon Cross was twice denied out wide, firstly by the Leeds defence and then by the referee after a looping pass from Tristan Sailor was ruled forward.

The hosts were reduced to 12 men when Daniel Suluka-Fifita was sinbinned for a late tackle on Presley Cassell, who had to leave the field for a head injury assessment, which he passed.

Leeds pushed again and Jack Bird went close to grounding a bouncing ball before Smith broke through the defence for a superb individual try.

The visitors added their third just before the interval as Newman finished off a sweeping move in the corner.

The Rhinos thought they had extended the lead further when Tom Holroyd crashed over soon after the restart but the video referee ruled the ball was not grounded.

It proved only a brief respite for Saints as Bird released Hall with a brilliant flick out of the back of his hand and the veteran winger slid over.

Saints finally registered as Jack Welsby broke clear from a Jonny Lomax pass and evaded a last-ditch tackle by Lachie Miller to score, with Sailor converting, but normal service was soon resumed.

Connor put boot to ball to create two more tries, dabbing a delicate grubber for Handley to touch down and then deliberately drilling a kick against the post for Croft to gather and score.

He converted both but failed to add to his tally late on when he hit the post from a penalty.

Huddersfield claim crucial win against play-off chasing Leigh

Huddersfield earned a vital win towards the foot of the table as they beat Leigh 30-18.

Cole Geyer scored twice as the Giants ran in five tries to move to 14 points and above second-bottom York.

Owen Trout gave visitors Leigh a perfect start as he scored the opening try in the 10th minute, with Adam Cook converting.

But the Giants, in danger at the wrong end of the division, levelled through Harry Rushton before Taane Milne crossed to give them a 14-6 half-time lead.

Niall Evalds' try after the restart gave them some breathing space before an end-to-end encounter followed.

Umyla Hanley brought the Leopards back into it with a 59th-minute try only for Geyer to score at the other end seven minutes later.

Robbie Mulhern scored another try for Leigh to keep the home nerves jangling, only for Geyer to bag his second try of the night to seal the win.

Catalans thrash Castleford after power cut!

Catalans Dragons game at Castleford was paused for 35 minutes during the second half due to a power outage before the visitors eventually ran out 34-6 winners.

Catalans climb to eighth in the table after a comfortable victory, with a pair of tries from Toby Sexton plus further scorers from Edenn Rogers-Smith, Leo Darrelatour, Ben Condon and Lewis Dodd.

Castleford were marking 100 years since their first match but it was a night to forget, with Lazarus Vaalepu scoring their only try in a dispiriting defeat.

Sexton touched down under the posts early on, after Darrelatour found him with a neat kick down the left. Rogers-Smith added a second try for Catalans, before Vaalepu crossed under the posts on his home debut.

Darrelatour then went over for his second try before, with the score at 16-6, the power went leading to a lengthy delay. When play resumed, a fine Charlie Staines drive set up Condon to ensure the game was put beyond Castleford before Dodd and Sexton added two more scores for good measure.

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+ .

articles.title: WWE SmackDown Winners, Live Grades, Reaction and Highlights From Aug. 28
articles.summary: Friday's SmackDown may not have been a go-home show before a premium live event, but it would put a heavy focus on hyping up Sunday Night's Main Event next weekend.
articles.body:
Friday's SmackDown may not have been a go-home show before a premium live event, but it would put a heavy focus on hyping up Sunday Night's Main Event next weekend.

CM Punk and Kevin Owens were set to address last week's title match that was ruined by Sami Zayn's interference, and Cody Rhodes was looking to deliver a message to Randy Orton.

In the women's division, Paige was poised to challenge Jacy Jayne for the U.S. title, while Tatum Paxley prepared to make her SmackDown in-ring debut against Michin. Elsewhere, Chelsea Green would team with Tiffany Stratton to take on Nia Jax and Lash Legend.

Let's take a look at what happened on this week's SmackDown at the Rocket Arena in Cleveland.

After a quick recap video, Kevin Owens made his way to the ring. He said he has lost a lot of title matches, but none of them were as bad to lose as last week.

As KO was talking about CM Punk, he arrived and told Owens he would have beaten him with or without Sami Zayn's interference.

Gunther showed up a moment later to make an argument for why he deserves a title shot. It didn't take long for Finn Balor to join the party.

Nick Aldis was already out there trying to keep the peace, so he decided to book a triple threat between Owens, Balor and Gunther for a title shot.

This was a pretty standard segment. Keeping it from boiling over also prevented it from being exciting, but it set up an interesting match for later in the show, so it accomplished its goal.

KO tried to hide a smile when the crowd started chanting.

Owens almost got a little choked up when talking about his mom's health.

Irresistible Forces vs. Chelsea Green and Tiffany Stratton

The first match of the night saw Nia Jax and Lash Legend face Chelsea Green and Tiffany Stratton. Before the match, Tiffy tried to tell Chelsea she didn't have to do this, but the champ had a protective mask to protect her eye, so she was up for it.

Stratton got in a few moves before tagging in Green, and they managed to maintain the upper hand after Jax tagged in, but only momentarily. The powerhouse countered the Unprettier and nailed her with a headbutt that Chelsea sold to make look like it reinjured her eye.

Tiffany was on the receiving end of a lot of offense during the break and into the next segment. Doctors came to check on Chelsea after she took another shot to the face and rolled out of the ring.

The story of this match was better than the execution. Green was great overselling her injury, and Stratton did a good job carrying the in-ring action, but the match itself lacked the needed energy until the end.

Green was being escorted away by doctors, but she ran back and tagged in when she saw Stratton suffering. Unfortunately, her injury was too much of a liability. Jax took advantage and hit her finisher for the win.

Result: Jax and Legend defeated Green and Stratton

The way Tiffany bumped right at the beginning of the match was so weird because Legend didn't do a thing to take her down. It almost looked like a missed dropkick, but she didn't get high enough for it to be that.

Legend has improved a lot since arriving in WWE a few years ago, but there are still moments when she seems to hesitate before moves.

The way Green was selling for her orbital bone was a little over the top, but it worked for her.

Paige vs. Jacy Jayne (United States Championship)

Paige had her first shot at a singles title since returning to WWE when she challenged Jacy Jayne for the United States Championship.

As usual, Fallon Henley and Lainey Reid were at ringside to give Jayne some backup, but Paige didn't seem intimidated by them.

The former world champion took control after Jayne scored the first takedown, and she stayed aggressive as they took the fight out of the ring, but that is where Reid was able to interfere with a pump kick while the ref was distracted.

Having Green and Stratton lose the previous match meant they were unable to assist Paige in any way, so even though she is a former champion, it never felt like the title was in danger of changing hands.

This match had a good pace and some decent action, but the predictability hurt its chances. Jayne won with an inside cradle after Paige had to fend off Henley and Reid. This wasn't a bad match, but it's hard to say it was memorable.

Nikki Bella attacked Paige after it was over, which was kind of surprising because it would have made more sense for her to cost Paige the win to prevent her from getting a belt, but the match already had enough interference, so holding back was probably the right call.

Danhausen being a Gunther fan was a funny backstage moment.

Jayne is so good at her facial expressions. She sells every moment perfectly, good or bad.

Reid's pump kick almost looked like it was in slow motion. She needs to put a little more speed on moves like that to make them look convincing.

Cody Rhodes came out to the ring to address what has been going on between him and Randy Orton since SummerSlam.

He talked about how Orton is his own worst enemy and has cost himself so many opportunities over the years. He said The Viper has been protected despite his screwups.

As expected, Orton came out to give his thoughts on the matter. He and Rhodes both looked like they wanted to rip each other's head off, but Orton grabbed a mic and decided to respond to what Rhodes said about him.

Orton did everything he could to get under Cody's skin, including mentioning his late dog, Pharoah. He took a few shots at Cody's family, too, but he wouldn't take the bait. He even turned it around and insulted Orton's dad.

Neither man would take the first shot, so the segment ended without violence, but it did a good job building tension for their showdown next weekend. Orton was especially good in this segment.

Baron Corbin had a quick backstage segment with Trick Williams, but there was no physical confrontation.

Orton has remained largely the same character for a long time, but there is no denying that he is good at it. He makes you pay attention even when he isn't saying anything new because he makes it interesting.

Before the match, Alexa Bliss and Charlotte Flair told Tatum Paxley that the three of them would face Jade Cargill, B-Fab and Michin at Sunday Night's Main Event next weekend, but first, Paxley had her SmackDown debut match against Michin.

To help keep things even, Flair and Bliss accompanied Paxley to the ring since Jade and B-Fab were in Michin's corner.

Tatum didn't look intimidated despite giving up a lot of experience. In fact, she looked almost emotionless at first. Neither woman could get a clear advantage until Michin nailed a kick from the apron.

While both Superstars went through the motions, there was a complete lack of intensity in this match. Even the moments that were supposed to feel that way fell flat. Nothing they did looked especially bad, but the match was listless.

Paxley scored the win with her finisher, but she had to make a quick exit to avoid Cargill and B-Fab.

Whatever Paxley whispered to Jackie Redmond backstage made Jackie run away.

Ricky Saints had a backstage segment with Rey Fenix asking for a shot at his cruiserweight title.

This week's main event was the triple threat that was booked in the opening segment with Owens, Gunther and Balor.

The match didn't get started until there was only about 12 minutes left in the show, so it felt like this might have an inconclusive finish before the bell even rang.

Gunther attacked Balor while he was entering the ring, so the match immediately got off to a hot start. All three men were moving quickly and trying to pack as much into the time they had as possible.

These are three skilled veterans, so there was little doubt that the match would be good. The important part was always going to be how it ended.

As it looked like Balor was going to get the win, Sami Zayn showed up and pulled him out of the ring. He dropped the referee, which also prevented KO from winning. When another ref ran down, Zayn took him out, too.

Punk ran down and started fighting with Zayn. The former champion took out everyone with the WWE title belt to be the last man standing.

Most of what we got here was good, but the ending left a lot to be desired. It obviously set things up for the future, but a no contest finish to the main event is never how you want to see a show end.

Giulia attacked Blake Monroe backstage to get revenge for last week.

Orton and Owens had a really funny moment backstage.

Danhausen and Kit Wilson appear to have gotten better after Danhausen's experiments.

When the best thing on an entire show is a non-wrestling segment with no physicality, it's going to leave a lot of people disappointed.

Friday's show was great for the women's division with three matches and a couple of backstage segments, but the best thing on the show was the exchange between Rhodes and Orton.

They sold the personal nature of their feud with a lot of enthusiasm, and holding back on another fight felt like the right decision in this case.

As far as in-ring action goes, the main event was the best match on the show, but the way it ended kept it from being the best segment overall.

It was a pretty weak episode overall, but it addressed several feuds and storylines, so it wasn't a total wash.

articles.title: Tua Tagovailoa leads TD drive and loses fumble in Falcons' 17-12 preseason win over Dolphins
articles.summary: Tua Tagovailoa led a touchdown drive but lost a fumble while playing the first quarter for Atlanta against his former team, and the Falcons beat the Miami Do...
articles.body:
MIAMI GARDENS, Fla. (AP) — Tua Tagovailoa led a touchdown drive but lost a fumble while playing the first quarter for Atlanta against his former team, and the Falcons beat the Miami Dolphins 17-12 on Friday night.

Tagovailoa was booed as he took the field and finished 7 of 8 for 95 yards while playing three series. The 28-year-old spent his first six seasons with Miami before the Dolphins released him in March.

On his first series, Tagovailoa led a 60-yard drive, capped by Brian Robinson Jr.'s 3-yard touchdown run for a 7-0 lead.

Tagovailoa fumbled the snap to start Atlanta's second drive and Miami recovered. His third drive also ended in a turnover when Dolphins linebacker Jackson Woodard recovered Robinson's fumble at the Miami 13.

He was replaced by Cooper Rush, who went 13 of 18 for 106 yards and a touchdown.

Michael Penix Jr., the Falcons' starter for nine games last season who returned to practice Monday , participated in warmups but didn't play. He had been sidelined since last November with a torn ACL in his left knee.

Riley Patterson kicked four field goals for the Dolphins, who didn't score a preseason touchdown after their opening drive against Washington on Aug. 14.

The Falcons (2-1) used a smattering of starters for limited plays while the Dolphins (0-3) went with reserves.

Starting tight end Kyle Pitts also played the first quarter, catching three passes for 59 yards for Atlanta.

Miami quarterback Malik Willis sat for the second consecutive week. He appeared only in the opening series at Washington.

After Patterson's 46-yard field goal early in the second, Rush connected with Jack Velling for a 3-yard TD pass to make it 14-3.

Patterson and Atlanta's Nick Folk exchanged field goals in the final two minutes of the first half.

Cam Miller started for the second consecutive week for Miami and went 7 of 16 for 71 yards. Mark Gronowski replaced Miller in the second half and went 4 of 8 for 97 yards. He also ran for 28 yards on four carries.

Miami had a chance to end its touchdown drought, but Theo Wease Jr. dropped Gronoski's pass in the end zone midway through the third quarter. The drive stalled and Patterson kicked his third field goal, a 26-yarder.

Falcons: At Pittsburgh in their season opener on Sept. 13.

Dolphins: Open the season at Las Vegas on Sept. 13.

articles.title: Pahokee football stuns Royal Palm on 75-yard 'Hail Mary' touchdown
articles.summary: Pahokee escaped upset with a miraculous 75-yard touchdown on the final play, stunning Royal Palm Beach.
articles.body:
ROYAL PALM BEACH — Corian Davis might want to get comfortable in the spotlight because his name is going to be everywhere this week.

Pahokee 's cornerback-turned-receiver delivered the play of the week, and perhaps the play of the year, Friday night with a stunning 75-yard 'Hail Mary' touchdown as time expired to lift the Blue Devils to a 16-14 victory over Royal Palm Beach.

Facing an upset loss, Pahokee stood at its own 25-yard line with 10.1 seconds remaining. Quarterback Braylon Peterson started a desperate final play, lateraling to Uzarus Boswell, who launched a pass downfield to Davis.

Davis hauled in the pass, slipped through would-be tacklers and zigzagged across the field before breaking free for the winning score.

By the time he crossed the goal line, the clock had long since hit triple zeroes, triggering a wild celebration from the Pahokee sideline and cementing the play's place among the most memorable moments in the program's storied history.

"That was electrifying, man," Pahokee coach Carlos Lammons said. "I've been playing ball for a while. Played in college, played in bowl games, high school, state championships, four in a row. Man, I don't think I've ever been a part of a play of that magnitude. And for it to go down like that, the kid had to go over top of two people, break two tackles, and sprint another 40 yards. Man, that was amazing."

"I think it can be," Lammons said. "I think it will be. I think it should be."

How a wild ending helped Pahokee avoid upset

Zyon Gilbert got the scoring started on defense for Pahokee, returning an interception for a touchdown in the first quarter to stake the Blue Devils to a 7-0 advantage.

That was the type of start many expected. And when Pahokee nearly scored again, fumbling inside Royal Palm Beach's 10 yard line, it was seen as a hiccup.

With Royal Palm fielding a team replacing its quarterback and lead running back from 2025 and with turnover on its defensive side of the roster, not many knew what to expect.

But the Wildcats responded with a touchdown pass to Demetrius Gibson and began to take control of the momentum, and suddenly the game very much reflected the full-moon sky hovering above.

The Wildcats would scored once more on a 58-yard punt return for a touchdown by Demetrice Rolle — and for a time, that appeared destine to be the play of the game.

Pahokee added a field goal, but was unable to put together a go-ahead drive as the clock ticked down late into the fourth quarter.

The Blue Devils got one more shot with fewer than 40 seconds left inside their own 10 yard line.

An incomplete pass. A desperate run by Peterson. Still, it looked like the story of Friday's game had been written.

Peterson, Boswell, and Davis rewrote it in a moment, turning the game on its side in a moment of both jubilation and heartbreak, an epitome of Friday Night Lights.

"To be honest, I really can't tell you what went on," Davis said. "All I can tell you that the quarterback made a good throw. There wasn't really that much time left on the bar. So somebody had to make a big play and I made that big play. And we're gonna keep on doing it the whole year, the whole season."

"My team they stayed in the game," he continued. "They didn't give up. We bent, but we ain't break."

Not bad for Corian Davis' first week on offense

The junior cornerback is accustomed to being a difference-maker on defense, but this was a new twist.

Corian Davis took reps on the offensive side of the ball for the first time this week. And yet, with the game on the line, Davis was always the intended receiver in the play drawn up by the coaches.

"We knew coming in this week that we're gonna need an extra playmaker on offense," Lammons said. "This guy is a playmaker. When we need him, we know where to bring him."

Not a bad start on offense. Not bad at all.

Alex Peterman is a high school sports reporter for The Palm Beach Post. He can be reached at apeterman@usatodayco.com.
