articles.body:
CHARLOTTE, N.C. (AP) — Rookie Miles Davis ran for a 1-yard touchdown, Ryan Fitzgerald kicked three field goals and the Carolina Panthers held on to defeat the Houston Texans 16-13 on Friday night in the preseason finale for both teams.

Panthers fourth-string quarterback Kyle Trask, who was signed during training camp following a hamstring injury to Haynes King in the Hall of Fame game, finished 19 of 28 for 147 yards with one interception and led four scoring drives for Carolina (3-1).

Mills ran for 34 yards on 11 carries and Anthony Tyus had 10 carries for 41 yards.

Brett Rypien completed 13 of 23 passes for 101 yards, including a late 6-yard touchdown pass to Zay Jones for the Texans (0-3). He also threw one interception.

Houston's last-ditch effort to take its first lead of the game ended when Jeremiah Moon sacked Rypien and forced a fumble and Cam Gill recovered with 54 seconds left.

Both offensive coordinators were extremely conservative on offense playing on a field that has been waterlogged by heavy rains in the hours leading up to the game.

Houston's Davis Mills and Carolina's Kenny Pickett started at quarterback, but neither could muster any points before being removed in the second quarter.

Mills finished 3 of 7 for 18 yards with one interception, while Pickett was 5 of 8 for 48 yards.

Gipson makes an impact for Panthers early

Panthers outside linebacker Trevis Gipson Sr. was a difference-maker early on, sacking Mills on the game's first possession and then pressuring him into throwing an interception to safety Lathan Ransom.

Gipson has played in 66 games during his first six seasons in the league, mostly on special teams.

The Panthers will open the season without starting offensive tackles Ickey Ekwonu (knee) and Taylor Moton (blood clots), leaving opportunities for some young players to earn a spot on the 53-man roster.

One of those is rookie Albert Reese IV, but he struggled against the Texans allowing four pressures and one sack.

Texans defensive lineman Solomon Byrd was helped off the field after his neck snapped back while trying to tackle Panthers tight end James Mitchell in the fourth quarter.

Texans: Host Buffalo in Sept 13 in season opener.

Panthers: Host Chicago on Sept. 13 in season opener.

articles.title: Cathedral Prep wins at Sharon for first time in 30 years
articles.summary: The Cathedral Prep Ramblers, aided by two early touchdowns, held on to win its first game at Sharon in 30 years.
articles.body:
SHARON — Avenging a football loss from 30 years ago wasn't on Cathedral Prep's emotional radar after its Aug. 28 game at Sharon.

The Ramblers still celebrated like that mattered.

Prep, which only won three games last year and sat out postseason play for the first time since 1997, took an early 13-point lead and then persevered for a 15-13 victory at Sharon Tiger Stadium.

Veteran head coach Mike Mischler, not one for hyperbole, said it ranked among the most satisfying wins in that role for his alma mater's program.

The first of Mischler's three tenures in charge of the Ramblers was 1998, which was two years after Prep last played at Sharon. The Tigers won 19-10.

Prep also beat a Sharon team that seeks to repeat as District 10's Class 3A champion.

This is a developing story that the Erie Times-News will continue to follow.

articles.title: 66-69 – Rangers get outclassed by Brewers in 6-1 loss
articles.summary: A blowout spiritually until it was a blowout literally
articles.body:
The Texas Rangers scored one run but the Milwaukee Brewers scored six runs.

I did not have much hope for the Rangers to beat the Brewers tonight and they lo and behold, they did not.

In fact, the Rangers trailed 2-0 after one inning and the writing was pretty much already on the wall. That the game remained close through much of the evening was only a mirage as the Rangers didn't collect their second hit of the night until the eighth inning, which is also when they had their one and only at-bat with RISP.

Despite being one mighty speculative swing away from tying the game for many innings, it never really felt like Texas was close to eclipsing the early scant deficit they found themselves in against baseball's best club. Eventually Milwaukee made even running into one a moot proposition as they displayed their superiority in the late innings.

After scoring their one run of the night on their first hit via a solo home run from No. 9 hitter Danny Jansen in the top of the third, the next Ranger to reach was Justin Foscue on an infield single with an out in the eighth inning. Following an out and a walk, Jansen grounded out to end Texas' first and only threat.

Meanwhile, Milwaukee had 14 hits. Perhaps the best thing you can say is tonight's starter Cody Bradford and the Rangers walked a tightrope to prevent this from turning into a disaster until much later than it seemed it would as the Brewers left eleven on base while going just 4-for-15 with RISP while Texas had two non-Jansen dinger base runners all night.

Player of the Game : Jansen's fifth home run of the season prevented the ignominy of a shutout loss.

Up Next : The Rangers and Brewers are back at it tomorrow evening with staff ace Cal Quantrill set to take the mound for Texas against LHP Shane Drohan for Milwaukee.

articles.title: Bucs rookie QB Jalon Daniels gets a surprise start but falters in preseason loss at Jaguars
articles.summary: Jalon Daniels’ chances of earning Tampa Bay’s backup quarterback job seemed to diminish in the team’s preseason finale, a 19-0 loss at Jacksonville on Friday...
articles.body:
Jalon Daniels' chances of earning Tampa Bay's backup quarterback job seemed to diminish in the team's preseason finale, a 19-0 loss at Jacksonville on Friday night in which neither side played starters.

After leading the Buccaneers to come-from-behind victories against the New York Jets and Kansas City , Daniels got a surprise start against the Jaguars. But he failed to generate much offense, with Tampa Bay punting on six of its first seven possessions. Daniels botched a snap to end the other and was sacked three times .

Daniels completed 8 of 15 passes for 57 yards in nearly three quarters. He also ran four times for 9 yards.

He didn't get much help from his receivers. Rookie Dean Patterson IV and third-year pro Kameron Johnson dropped third down passes to end the first two drives and then Garrett Greene let one slip through his fingertips in the second quarter.

Getting the start was a chance for Daniels to show he was ready to supplant Jake Browning behind Baker Mayfield. Daniels is an undrafted rookie from Kansas who had been listed behind Browning and Connor Bazelak on Tampa Bay's depth chart.

Jacksonville got better results from its second-team quarterback, Nick Mullens. Trevor Lawrence's backup completed 5 of 7 passes for 62 yards in the first quarter.

"They set a tone early on, had some good drives and just (didn't) finish with some scores," Jaguars coach Liam Coen said.

Carter Bradley, the son of former Jaguars coach Gus Bradley, took over from there and misfired on two deep passes that could have been touchdowns. Bradley connected with DeeJay Dallas for a score late in the third and then scrambled for a 2-point conversion.

Cam Little kicked a 61-yard field goal, and rookie Michael Wortham returned a punt 63 yards for a TD late.

Rookie pass rushers shine for the Jaguars

Jacksonville is looking for additional pass rushers behind Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker. Rookies Wesley Williams and Bryan Thomas Jr. showed they're ready to contribute.

Williams, a fourth-round draft pick from Duke, nearly sacked Daniels on one play and recovered his fumble on another. Thomas, an undrafted rookie from South Carolina, finished with 2 1/2 sacks. They join second-year pro B.J. Greene II and veteran Dennis Gardeck in giving the Jags quality depth behind two big-time starters.

Jacksonville coach Liam Coen called his first plays of the preseason and then turned the job over to his offensive assistants.

Coen let offensive coordinator Grant Udinski call plays in the team's first two preseason games but reclaimed the role for the finale to get in a few reps before the regular season. Coen called plays in the first half against Tampa Bay and then relinquished the role to quarterbacks coach Spencer Whipple for the third quarter and pass game specialist John Van Dam for the fourth.

Coen did the same on the defensive side of the ball, with Mathieu Araujo, Tem Lukabu and Matt Edwards getting chances.

Buccaneers linebacker Mohamed Kamara was helped to the locker room in the third quarter with an apparent left knee injury.

Jaguars tight end Hunter Long was shaken up in the first quarter after Bucs safety Miles Killebrew delivered a big hit at the end of a 13-yard gain. Long caught two passes for 47 yards in the frame, putting together solid tape in case he doesn't make the team.

Tampa Bay opens the season at Cincinnati on Sept. 13.

Jacksonville hosts Cleveland on Sept. 13.

articles.title: Jaguars close out preseason with win over Buccaneers
articles.summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars finished the preseason with a win at home. Here are our takeaways.
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars have officially finished the 2026 preseason.

The Jaguars defeated the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 19-0. Several starters watched from the sideline as end-of-roster players were given the spotlight, getting one final chance to make an impression on the coaching staff ahead of cut down day on Aug. 30.

Head coach Liam Coen said earlier in the week that the team would leave the door open for any player who had a standout performance, but he admitted it's largely a decision made based on the body of work this offseason.

Photos: Jaguars wrap up home preseason schedule against Buccaneers

Did any players help their stock in the contest? Here are a few takeaways from the final preseason game:

Bryan Thomas Jr. does all he can to help roster chances

There were only a few roster spots available going into the contest. The Jaguars were largely set at several positions as they retained a majority of their team from the previous season.

Still, as Coen said, the door was open for any players to have a standout performance. Rookie undrafted free agent defensive lineman Bryan Thomas Jr. took full advantage of his opportunity.

Thomas logged 2.5 sacks in the game, terrorizing Tampa Bay's reserve offensive line and quarterbacks. He's come on strong in the final weeks of training camp and looked like he belonged in the final game.

It was similar to the performance by former undrafted free agent BJ Green last season in the final preseason game. That resulted in Green making the roster and he's projected to get play time with the starting defense this season.

We'll have to wait until Sunday to determine if he's on the roster or not, but it was a good performance by the undrafted free agent. One of several in recent weeks for him.

Michael Wortham scores on a punt return touchdown

Michael Wortham scored a 63-yard punt return touchdown in the fourth quarter, putting the game out of reach for the visitors.

Wortham got close to breaking free on an earlier return, but was tackled by punter Riley Dixon before he could elude him. He didn't let his next opportunity pass him by.

He caught the ball and back juked to avoid a nearby defender almost immediately. After regaining his balance he sped toward the left side of the field, accelerating past Buccaneers as teammates cleared a path for him.

Escorted by a teal convoy, he sped down the home sideline and made it to the endzone with ease. The undrafted free agent celebrated the touchdown surrounded by teammates, closing what's been an impressive offseason for him.

With how loaded the Jaguars are at receiver it's unlikely he'll be retained as a practice squad player after roster cuts, but after scoring a touchdown maybe another team will find value for him on their roster as a returner.

Cam Little remains automatic in the preseason

The Jaguars struck gold when they landed kicker Cam Little in the 2024 NFL Draft. He netted a 61-yard field goal in the first half to open the scoring for the game.

It brought his total to 20 of 21 field goals in his career in preseason games. His only miss was from 62 yards in his rookie season. He also hit a record 70-yarder in the 2025 preseason.

He's been one of the best players on the roster and his consistency has become a dependable aspect of Jacksonville's offense, giving the team confidence that they can end most drives with points.

Practice squad quarterback battle goes down to the wire

Obviously, the Jaguars are set at starting quarterback. The team will roll with Nick Mullens as the backup behind Trevor Lawrence.

But the starting practice squad quarterback spot has been up for grabs all training camp. Carter Bradley is the incumbent and has had an up-and-down performance in the preseason. He completed 8 of 15 passes for 77 yards and a touchdown against the Buccaneers, getting the chance to play in the second and third quarters.

He orchestrated a 14 play, 79-yard drive that resulted in Jacksonville's first touchdown of the game. Then he scored a two-point conversion to cap his night, diving in the endzone after faking out a Tampa Bay defender.

Aguilar had several drives stall out, but his near-perfect performance in the game against the Panthers and long pass against the Saints will certainly give the coaching staff to talk about.

It'll be a battle of experience versus potential and the winner will get the chance to man the scout team.

articles.summary: Buchholz and Gainesville High played on a different week this season, but the result remained the same as the Bobcats laid a running clock on their rival.
articles.body:
The date changed, the players wore different numbers, but the annual city rivalry game between Buchholz football and Gainesville High looked the same Friday night.

Buchholz defeated GHS 43-6 Friday night at Citizens Field to begin the 2026 season 2-0. The Hurricanes fell to 0-2 in Ashour Peera's opening campaign. The win, which was BHS' eighth in a row, set a new record in the rivalry.

It was clear from the first play that the result was going to be same.

Buchholz took the ball after winning the opening kick and marched down for a 10 play, 78 yard drive that ended in an Ashton Norris one yard run.

The Hurricanes, despite possessing first team All-Area running back and Eastside transfer Javaris Gardner, never held a chance offensively.

Buchholz-Vanguard Week 1 football showdown goes to OT. See the top photos.

They backed up 12 yards on their first series, and the snap on the punt was high. The Bobcats secured it for a touchdown.

From then on, the route was on. Dominick Harvey – a transfer from Hawthorne – caught two touchdowns from Andrew Whittemore and Josh Menefee scored a grown man touchdown.

That, plus a safety, put the game in running clock position before halftime with BHS up 36-0.

Buchholz emptied its bench in the second half with the running clock. A 20 yard Javaris Gardner touchdown broke the shutout and was the first points scored in a city rivalry game by GHS since the 2024 battle vs. the Bobcats.

articles.title: Instant Analysis: Falcons club Dolphins in final preseason game
articles.summary: Atlanta finishes preseason with easy win over Miami on the road
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons have won their preseason finale on the road against the Miami Dolphins , 17-12.

Of course preseason wins only matter to the Baltimore Ravens - everyone else uses these games to evaluate their players and decide who should be starting and who should make their initial 53-man rosters.

Let's review how the Falcons did in all three phases against a Miami team that's expected to be at the bottom of the AFC standings at the end of the year.

Tua Tagovailoa got booed by the Dolphins fanbase when he came out for his first possession, but he soon put them on quiet mode. After a quick dump-off to Jahan Dotson for 11 yards he found tight end Kyle Pitts on a quick-hitter, which ended in a 37-yard gain. A couple of handoffs to Brian Robinson Jr. later, and the Falcons were in the end zone for an early lead.

Tua only stayed on the field for a couple more drives, both of which ended in turnovers. First, backup center Corey Levin fumbled a snap that officially went on Tagovailoa's record, then Robinson fumbled on a rush which was recovered by the Dolphins. Nevertheless, the Falcons led 7-3 at the end of the first quarter when Tagovailoa left the game.

Cooper Rush came in next, and he was able to slice up the backups for the projected worst team in the league this year. He went 13/18 for 106 yards, one touchdown and a 105.3 passer rating, setting Atlanta up for a field goal and a 17-6 lead going into the locker room at halftime.

While their passing game was working most of the evening, the Falcons were unable to get their run game off the ground. Brian Robinson led them with just 15 yards on five carries and they average just 20 yards on 11 carries (1.8 YPC) in the first half. The Falcons ended the outing with just 41 rushing yards on 24 attempts.

Rookie Jack Strand came in at quarterback to begin the second half but barely saw any work in the third quarter, going 2/2 for 11 yards. He technically threw one interception, but it was off a deflection and not his fault. Strand finished the game 6/7 for 43 yards and no touchdowns.

The Falcons decided to play their starting defense against Miami's backups on offense on the first possession of the game, which ended how you would hope. Cam Miller and the Dolphins went backwards on their opening drive, which ended in a three-and-out courtesy of some bullying up front from Brandon Dorlus and Samson Ebukam.

Atlanta's defense continued to push the Dolphins around until halftime, with Cameron Thomas and rookie linebacker Harold Perkins Jr. notching sacks against Miller. They also were able to contain Miami's run game, limiting the Dolphins' backs to just 21 rushing yards and 2.6 yards per attempt in the first half.

The Dolphins got some momentum with their run game in the third quarter, but Atlanta's defense held up, keeping them out of the end zone through three quarters, still leading 17-9.

In the end, the Falcons tallied five sacks, eight QB hits and seven tackles for a loss all together. They held the Dolp[hins to just 236 total yards.

The Falcons got another solid game out of their punt returners, with Dylan Drummond and Zachariah Branch both going for 18 on their best respective attempts. Rookie Vinny Anthony II had the biggest kickoff return of the evening, posting a 52-yarder late in the game.

Meanwhile, Nick Folk made his only field goal from 34 yards out and Jake Bailey totaled 281 yards on five punts.

articles.title: Kentucky vs Youngstown State Prediction: Welcome to the New UK
articles.summary: New coach, new players, new all-around attitude with high expectations. Kentucky wants to turn things around fast, and it starts against Youngstown State.
articles.body:
Kentucky has been the working definition of an also-ran over the last several years, and it's up to new head coach Will Stein to change that. The former Oregon offensive coordinator cranked up the transfer portal, brought in a slew of good weapons, and now the Wildcats are about to look far different. It starts against a Youngstown State team with a terrific ground game and with a win under its belt.

Kentucky vs Youngstown State: Quick Hits

Youngstown State ran all over Mercyhurst with a 43-10 win. It's a dangerous team that will push the UK defense.

Kentucky will likely start eight transfers on offense, including Notre Dame transfer quarterback Kenny Minchey.

The Wildcats have won five straight season openers and eight of the last nine.

How To Watch Kentucky vs Youngstown State

Date: Saturday, September 5, 2026 Game Time: 1:00 pm ET TV: SEC Network Location: Kroger Field, Lexington, KY – CFN Week 1 Schedule, Predictions

The running game is dangerous. Great throughout last year, the Penguins started this season averaging seven yards per carry with over 250 yards rolled up on Mercyhurst. They have a deep backfield, but quarterback Beau Brungard is the one who makes it all go. He's a do-it-all playmaker who gets to deal with a questionable Kentucky defensive front. The Wildcats are 0-10 over the last two years when allowing 145 rushing yards or more. Youngstown State averaged 202 per game last season.

The offense will work right away. Youngstown State will be plucky, and it has a decent enough defensive front to bother Minchey, but the Cats will look different. They'll be faster, more balanced, and with the explosion that's been missing over the last several seasons. And yes, the defensive front is getting some reworking, but helped by the addition of Hasaan Sykes (Western Carolina) and Jordan Castell (Florida), the secondary is loaded.

Kentucky vs Youngstown State Prediction, Betting Lines

This is a good matchup to get Kentucky rolling. Youngstown State will have its moments, but that's a good thing. The Wildcats will have to keep pushing and won't be able to put it on cruise control. There won't be any real drama, though, with the UK offense taking over in a terrific third quarter. Minchey will be great.

articles.title: Harris homer leads Braves’ hit parade as Braves win 80th game and series opener versus the Rockies
articles.summary: Ronald Acuña Jr. thrived in the cleanup spot, going 3-for-3 with a walk.
articles.body:
You can't get a high-octane, 1-0 complete game every night. The series opener for Braves-Rockies was always bound to feel different than this last few nights versus Los Angeles, and boy, did it deliver on that front.

The swing-happy Rockies collected eleven singles and one double off of the Braves pitching staff. But the Braves weren't going to be outdone Friday at home, where they've been dominant. They outhit and outscored the Rockies by two for fourteen hits and a final score of 6-4 to secure their 80th win of the season.

It was a quiet first frame as each starter began the game with a 1-2-3 inning. Grant Holmes issued a leadoff walk to TJ Rumfield followed by a single to Willi Castro, but got out of it with a Mickey Moniak lineout and a Connor Norby double play.

"Cleanup man" may just be the psychological trick needed to get Ronald Acuña Jr. going. He led off two innings anyway, but the reset / new mentality seemed to make all the difference as he ended up 3-for-3 on the evening. His great night began with a leadoff walk in the second. He then scored from first on a double off the bat of Michael Harris II, giving the Braves a 1-0 lead.

Mauricio Dubón's productive out moved Harris to third before Mike Yastrzemski battled for nine pitches before he whiffed for strike three. But Harris wouldn't be stranded – Sean Murphy, in a bit of deja vu from Wednesday, laced one down the third base line juuust fair for a double to make it 2-0.

Don't look now, but Ha-Seong Kim has now reached base three straight games after being hit by a pitch. We take those.

Drake Baldwin drove in his fellow catcher on a single to center field to extend the lead to 3-0 before Ozzie Albies flew out to end the inning. A crooked number for the Bravos? Is that allowed?

Holmes worked around a Zac Veen leadoff single in the top of the third before setting down the next three Rockies in order.

Ronald's first hit of the night came in the bottom of the third with a single to center field. He advanced to second on a Harris sac bunt and scored on a Dubón single.

Your browser does not support the video tag. Download the video .

Holmes allowed a couple more singles in the top of the fourth, but a nice Ozzie/Kim play and two other groundouts helped him escape.

Grant was not so fortunate in the top of the fifth. Consecutive singles by Veen (again) and shortstop Ezequiel Tovar set the table for Jake McCarthy's sac fly to end the shutout and make it 4-1.

Two more singles by Cole Carrigg and Hunter Goodman kept the line moving. Seemingly aware it was not our usual infielders and alignments, there was a weird vortex that appeared between Dubón at third and Ha-Seong Kim at short. Goodman's hit deflected off of both of their gloves before rolling into left field.

All of a sudden, Colorado had chipped away enough to make it a one-run ballgame at 4-3. Holmes settled down to get Castro to fly out and end the fifth, closing the book on tonight's outing: 8 hits (all singles), 3 earned runs, 1 walk, and 3 strikeouts on 84 pitches.

But the Braves would get some of those runs right back. Our outfielders combined for our first multi-run home run in a while: Ronald doubled to right, and once again got to trot home to score on a blast to the Chophouse by Money Mike. Dubón's single prompted Warren Schaeffer to make a pitching change.

Tomoyuki Sugano exited to the dulcet tones of Ke$ha proclaiming that this place was "about to blow". With the field awash in red light, Mark Manfredi entered to stop the Braves from adding on any further. He struck out pinch-hitter Lane Thomas, got Murph to fly out sharply to center, and Kim to pop out to short to end the rally with the Braves leading 6-3.

Dylan Dodd allowed a leadoff double to Moniak to start the sixth, but put up another zero with a swinging strikeout and two flyouts.

After a Baldwin lineout and Ozzie taking a risk on a hustle double that did not work out, Matt Olson finally decided to join the party with a single to right, followed by Ronald's second single. But Manfredi got Harris to line out sharply to left to end the sixth, keeping the Braves off the board for his two innings of relief.

Ray Kerr entered to face the top of the Rockies order in what ended up being an eventful seventh inning. He hit McCarthy and got Carrigg to fly out. But a single to Goodman and a walk by Rumfield loaded the bases, prompting a mound visit from Jeremy Hefner. Castro's sac fly made it 6-4 before Moniak's strikeout ended the inning.

Murphy hit a two-out single off new reliever Juan Mejia in the bottom of the seventh, but nothing else of note occured.

Victor Mederos jogged out of the bullpen for the eighth inning. Veen worked a walk between Norby groundout and flyout by pinch-hitter Troy Johnston. But a McCarthy single put runners at the corners. A diving play by Ozzie / flip to Olson on a ground ball hit by Carrigg was challenged by Colorado. We all braced for the replay center to overturn the out call and allow the Rockies to add another run, but New York was on our side for this one (!) and we moved right on along. The home half of the eighth ended expeditiouisly as Brennan Bernardino set down our top three in order.

Raisel Iglesias came into the ninth with the two-run lead and set to face the heart of the Rockies order. Team home run leader Goodman did not hit a dinger, thankfully, but a freak single off his bat allowed him to reach. But our own home run leader can also pick it with the best of them – Olson started a beautiful double play to send Goodman and Rumfield back to the visiting dugout and bring Castro up as the last hope for the Rockies.

More defensive magic in the form of an Ozzie Albies diving play for out number three sealed this one for the Braves.

With a final score of 6-4, that extends Atlanta's win streak to five games, is the 80th win of the season, and improves the Braves' home record to 46-23, which is the best in baseball. Most excitingly? Every Brave except Lane Thomas (who had two ABs after hitting in Yaz's spot) and Ha-Seong Kim had a hit tonight. Here's hoping that this upward offensive trend continues.

The Braves will return to action tomorrow afternoon with Martin Perez on the mound for the 4:10 pm ET start.

articles.title: Jaguars preseason stock report after final game: Who's up, who's down?
articles.summary: Following the Jaguars' final preseason game, which players gave their roster stock a big boost and which players went the opposite direction?
articles.body:
Friday night's win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers wraps up the 2026 training camp and preseason schedule for the Jacksonville Jaguars .

Next up for GM James Gladstone is roster cutdown day, which is Sunday. By 6:00 PM ET that day, the Jaguars roster must be whittled down to 53 players.

Over the last month of practices and games, several players have given their stock a boost, while a few others went in the opposite direction. Here's a look at who those players are.

Abdullah has provided a steady presence out of the backfield this summer, impacting the game both as a ball carrier and as a pass catcher. He also has return experience as well. His play has put him in the mix for a roster spot if the Jaguars choose to keep a fourth running back. With LeQuint Allen sidelined at the moment, Abdullah could contribute on passing downs.

Braswell's role on defense expanded as the 2025 season went on, to the point that he was seeing regular snaps during the second half of the year. However, up-and-down play in training camp seemingly has his roster spot in jeopardy, with Jabbar Muhammad passing Braswell on the depth chart. In two preseason games, Braswell had allowed 8 completions on 11 targets for 79 yards with no ball production. He did have a better outing against Tampa Bay but was it enough to make the team?

A late riser this training camp, it looked like for much of the summer that Pregnon was going to fill a backup role, but he now appears to be in line to start at left guard in Week 1. Offensive coordinator Grant Udinski recently praised Pregnon for his play.

Stock down: TE Quintin Morris and Hunter Long

From the jump, both were immediately passed by rookie Tanner Koziol on the depth chart. And with one roster spot potentially up for grabs at tight end, neither has been able to stand out and secure that spot. It's possible that the Jaguars keep only three tight ends, which means both Morris and Long would be released.

Rotational snaps behind Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker were up for grabs this summer, and Green's steadiness in both the run and pass games may have earned him that third spot on the depth chart. He flashed some playmaking potential as well.

articles.title: Big hit eludes Rockies as Braves win series opener 6-4
articles.summary: Rockies tally plenty of hits but go 1-for-11 with men in scoring position
articles.body:
After splitting a series against the Washington Nationals, the Colorado Rockies looked to start the series in Atlanta on a high note. Despite a solid night offensively, the Rockies left a small village on the base paths as the big hit eluded them and couldn't keep pace with a dangerous Braves offense.

Hoping to break a string of difficult starts, the cards were not in Tomoyuki Sugano's (菅野 智之) favor against the Braves. Things looked promising as Sugano worked a quick 1-2-3 first inning, a far cry from the 45 pitches he threw in his last outing. Unfortunately for Sugano, the Braves picked away at him in the second inning to build a 3-0 lead.

Ronald Acuña Jr. led off with a walk and came in to score on a double from Michael Harris II. After Maricio Dubón flew out, advancing Harris to third base, and Mike Yastrzemski struck out, Sean Murphy delivered an RBI double down the line to score another run. Ha-Seong Kim was then hit by a pitch, setting the table for Drake Baldwin to shoot a ball up the middle to score a third run.

Dubón added another RBI single in the third inning to increase the lead to 4-0. Sugano managed a harmless fourth inning, and his offense closed the deficit in the top of the fifth inning, but his night would be over after just three batters when he came back out to pitch. Acuña smoked the first pitch he saw all the way to the wall for a double, and then Harris launched a two-run home run on the second pitch of the inning to give the Braves a 6-3 lead. Dubón's single delivered the final blow to knock Sugano out of the game.

Once again, Sugano's command eluded him. Due to the Atlanta heat and humidity, he struggled to grip the baseball and ended up having to rely on his fastball much more than usual. As a result, he threw 91 pitches, 58 strikes, and allowed six runs on 10 hits with four strikeouts and one walk. He wasn't able to dip into his secondaries and was often working behind hitters, and the contact started to get harder and harder by the time that fifth inning rolled around.

"He got behind in the count again," manager Warren Schaeffer said. "Not a lot executed tonight. Got hit pretty hard there. It's just been a tough couple of times out for Tomo."

The Rockies bullpen has continued to do their job and pick up quite a bit of slack from the rotation and this game was no different.

Mark Manfredi relieved Sugano in the fifth inning and continued to impress in his young career . He ended up throwing two solid innings, giving up just three hits and striking out one batter. He was then replaced by Juan Mejia, who tossed a scoreless inning, allowing just one hit. Brennan Bernardino then faced the minimum in the eighth inning.

They combined for just four hits over four innings on 49 total pitches.

Once again, the Rockies found themselves searching for the big hit in the game on offense. In the second inning, the Rockies had something promising after TJ Rumfield walked and Willi Castro singled to put runners on first and second against Grant Holmes. Mickey Moniak smoked a liner to first base that was snagged by Matt Olson for the first out. Connor Norby then grounded into a double play to end the inning.

In the fourth inning, Rumfield singled and was then replaced on the bases by Castro after he grounded into a fielder's choice. Moniak singled to put men on the corners, but Norby grounded out to end the threat once again.

They finally broke through in the fifth inning against Holmes when Zac Veen, who recorded his first multi-hit game, singled to lead off the inning and advanced to third on a base hit from Ezequiel Tovar. Jake McCarthy got the Rockies on the board with a sacrifice fly to center field. Cole Carrigg tallied a base hit and Tovar came in to score the Rockies' second run on a single by Hunter Goodman. The third run of the inning came when Rumfield grounded out to the shortstop, allowing Carrigg to score from third.

The string of hits made it a one-run game at the time before the Harris home run in the bottom half of the inning. It also ended Holmes's night after the fifth inning as he allowed three runs on eight hits with three strikeouts and one walk.

"All year… we pass the baton," Schaeffer said. "That's why our offense is so much better this year. Selfless baseball, just trying to get on for the next guy, that's what we do."

Facing the dangerous Braves bullpen, the Rockies threatened Ray Kerr in the seventh inning, but couldn't get the big hit to shift the momentum of the game. McCarthy was hit by a pitch, Goodman singled, and Rumfield walked to load the bases with one out. Castro sent the first pitch he saw to center field for a sacrifice fly to give the Rockies their fourth run of the game. Unfortunately, the Rockies couldn't get more as the left-on-left matchup for Moniak resulted in a strikeout to end the inning.

The eighth inning continued the theme on offense. Veen drew a one-out walk and moved up to third on a two-out single by McCarthy. With men on the corners and two outs, Carrigg ripped a ball to second base that was gathered by Ozzie Albies. Carrigg flew down the line, forcing a bang-bang play at the bag, and was called out. The Rockies challenged, but the call was upheld, ending the inning.

Goodman secured his third hit of the night with a single in the ninth off of Raisel Iglesias, but was quickly erased on a double-play. Castro then lined out softly courtesy of a diving catch by Albies to end the game. That was a common trend on the night as well, as the Braves continued to make some impressive defensive plays to rob the Rockies of hits that could have drastically altered the game for them.

Despite the 12 hits, the Rockies ended up going 1-for-11 with runners in scoring position, leaving 10 men on base. They have now gone 2-for-20 over the last two games. They only struck out five times and had three walks, with the only extra-base hit being Moniak's double in the sixth.

"We had chances all night; I thought we swung the bats well, " said Schaeffer. "We got after it offensively; we came back, kept the foot on the gas. Just didn't get the job done."

The Rockies and Braves continue the series Friday, with Ryan Feltner (5-8, 6.08 ERA) facing veteran lefty Martín Pérez (8-8, 3.12 ERA).

First pitch is scheduled for 2:10 pm MDT. See you then!

articles.summary: NBA fans are hyped to see the Lakers' new power forward Sandro Mamukelashvili's impressive performance against Montenegro in the 2026 FIBA qualifiers.
articles.body:
Sandro Mamukelashvili is currently one of several NBA players on international duty for the second round of the FIBA Qualifiers this week. The Lakers' new addition pulled off an impressive performance in Georgia's 101-74 win over Montenegro.

The Georgian power forward stuffed the box score as he finished with 17 points, seven rebounds, six assists, and two steals, while shooting 6-13 from the field (46.2 FG%) and 2-5 from behind the three-point line (40.0 3P%).

The Lakers fans were fired up to see Mamukelashvili's impressive display, which included elite vision and playmaking. After seeing the newest Lakers player's performance, they took to social media and flooded it with praise for the 27-year-old.

"The Lakers really got a center version of Luka Doncic 😭🔥"

"Bro is basically Luka in a center's body 😭🔥 The Lakers found a cheat code! 🏀💀"

"Mamu with a crazy no-look dime to find his teammate for a dunk 🤯"

He didn't just impress the Lakers' fans with his playmaking, but also with his tough finishes inside the paint on transition.

"That's a grown-a** man right there, gaddamn."

"My backup tweener big can dribble, pass, shoot, and he's a demon transition scorer with a three ball 💕 I actually can't wait to watch him this year."

In 2025-26, Mamukelashvili ended the season averaging 11.2 points, 4.9 rebounds and 1.9 assists while shooting 52.3% from the field and 38.9% from the three-point range for the Raptors in a limited role.

It was initially expected that the Lakers would play him at power forward to replace Rui Hachimura in the starting lineup . However, given the Lakers' lack of offseason moves, he is also expected to play backup center behind Walker Kessler and Kevon Looney.

The 6'9″ forward is a perfect player to run a potential small-ball lineup to space the floor and provide an outside shooting threat instead of clogging the paint. That will give a lot more room for slashers to cut inside the paint for a lob threat that Luka Doncic is known to capitalize on.

The Lakers supporters now have even more reason to be thrilled about Mamukelashvili's arrival thanks to his outstanding performance for Georgia. He may be one of the roster's versatile players due to his size, shooting, playmaking, and ability to finish through contact. His skill set offers the Lakers valuable lineup flexibility, especially when paired with Luka Doncic, even though his exact role is still unknown.

Mamukelashvili could easily become a fan favorite and give Los Angeles a special offensive weapon that can make an impact at several positions if he can maintain this confidence throughout the NBA season.

articles.title: Bears Preseason: Could a big game by Jamree Kromah secure a roster spot?
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears defensive line needs difference makers, so could a big game by Jamree Kromah secure a roster spot?
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears' offseason has seen several players raise their stock. None more so than sixth-round draft pick Jordan van den Berg, who went from a fun athletic day-three prospect to getting reps with the starters. At this point, van den Berg's roster spot is a lock, but there's another defensive lineman who made a splash in the last couple of weeks.

Jamree Kromah came out of college in 2024 as one of the most athletic defensive tackles in his class ( 9.67 RAS ), but he went undrafted and signed with the Bears. He moved up and down the line at James Madison, but as a pro his future was at defensive end. The 275-pounder had a nice camp and totaled 3 tackles and 2 QB hits in the preseason and was ultimately signed to Chicago's practice squad.

The New England Patriots signed him to their active roster a couple of weeks later, but he was waived and signed back to the Bears' practice squad, where he remained the rest of 2024.

He was back in Chicago the next year, and in the 2025 preseason he had 6 tackles and a QB hit. The Bears once again signed him to the practice squad, where he stayed all season.

"One thing I did for sure was I changed my body, changed my nutrition, because I was much heavier last year," Kromah said in the locker room following the preseason opener against the Browns, where he hit the D-lineman trifecta of a sack, forced fumble, and recovery all on the same play. "So I wanted to make some changes by losing weight. I lost over 20 pounds, but got stronger and then put more lean mass on. So this is the best I have felt … I had to look at the man in the mirror and be true to myself, and come up with a real plan."

In his first two preseason games, the 6'3″, now 268-pounder, has 6 tackles, 3 tackles for loss, 2 sacks, and a forced fumble and fumble recovery. His second game wasn't as impactful, but he did have a half-sack negated by a holding penalty.

In Saturday's game in Tennessee, he'll get another chance to shine and make a final push for a roster spot. The Bears may not play their starters, but starting defensive end Austin Booker is sidelined with a groin issue, which could create more opportunities for Kromah.

Our friends at FanDuel Sportsbook currently have the Titans as a 2.5 point favorite in the preseason finale. If you think the Bears will win outright, the moneyline is at +122, with the point total over/under at 37.5.

The Miami Dolphins have completed their 2026 NFL Preseason schedule with a loss to the Atlanta Falcons on Friday night. The Falcons game, along with their earlier games against the Washington Commanders and New York Giants, and the summer's training camp practices, have given the Dolphins' coaches all the evaluations they need to build the team's roster for this year – and they now have to start making decisions.

The NFL roster cuts deadline is fast approaching. Miami and all 31 other teams must cut from the preseason 90-man roster to the regular-season limit of 53 players over the next couple of days. Roster cuts are due by 6 p.m. Eastern on Sunday, August 30.

After the cuts, practice squad players will sign or re-sign with the team. We will track those on Monday, but each team can carry up to 16 additional reserve and developmental players.

The final 53-man roster is, of course, anything but final. Players will be re-signed, claimed off waivers, or signed as free agents before the season begins on Wednesday, September 9. Even after the regular season kicks off, we will see plenty of roster moves, especially for Miami who will likely churn the bottom of the roster all season long.

The 2026 season is not expected to be a good one for the Dolphins. According to the oddsmakers at FanDuel Sportsbook, Miami has the longest odds to make the playoffs in the AFC at +1500 . The New York Jets have the next worst odds at +700. Miami's roster churn will, hopefully, help the Dolphins find players who can grow with the team as they move through this year's rebuild and into the 2027 season and beyond.
